3	/// Remove Silences' detector (road map 2 phase 3a): the quiet spans of a
4	/// project, as project-time ranges the core's `ripple_delete_ranges` cuts.
5	///
6	/// **It reads the PLAN, not the peaks alone.** A bucket in
7	/// `cache/peaks/<media id>.bin` is a PRE-FADER magnitude — the file's own
8	/// loudness, knowing nothing about `volume`, a fade, a duck, a mute or a
9	/// solo. What the user means by "silent" is what they HEAR, so the level this
10	/// asks about is `peak × envelope`, and the envelope is the one the core
11	/// already published: `CompositionPlan`'s audio tracks carry `segments` (what
12	/// sound plays, from which file, from which source offset, over which project
13	/// span, already clamped to the file by `evaluate.rs`) and `ramps` (the
14	/// envelope over the track's whole extent, fades, volume actions and ducking
15	/// folded in).
16	///
17	/// That one decision is what keeps mute and solo out of this file. `audio.rs`
18	/// expresses both as a ZERO envelope rather than as an absent segment — by
19	/// deliberate design, so that unmuting never rebuilds the composition — which
20	/// means a muted clip is quiet here for free, with no second Swift copy of
21	/// `audio.rs`'s `silenced` to drift from the first.
22	///
23	/// **A nest is a wall, not a place to cut inside.** The plan FLATTENS a nest
24	/// into one segment per clip inside it (`core/src/nest.rs`), so the sound
25	/// measured over a nest clip is its CONTENTS' and nothing in the plan says
26	/// so — `segment.clip` is the inner clip's id and `snapshot.clip` cannot
27	/// find it. That is a trap, because `Source::Nest` has no in point: a nest
28	/// clip always plays its nest from the first frame, so splitting one leaves
29	/// two clips that each replay it from the top with the middle unreachable.
30	/// `ripple_delete_ranges` splits every unlocked track at both of a span's
31	/// bounds, so a candidate that reached into a nest would not take the dead
32	/// air out of it — it would strand its tail. A nest's sound therefore still
33	/// PROTECTS a span, exactly as any other sound does (it is what the ear
34	/// hears, and a loud nest keeps a tick out of a run), but no candidate may
35	/// INTERSECT one: `Input.nests` is the list of walls and `excludingNests`
36	/// cuts every run against them. **The dead air inside a nest is reached by
37	/// OPENING it** (⌘↓, or `set_scope`) — `Input.read` takes its snapshot and
38	/// its plan off `editedProject`, so with a nest open the walls are the ones
39	/// inside it and the runs are its own. Road map 2's phase 9 made that the
40	/// everyday path; the round trip (⇧⌘G, cut, ⌘G) still works and is no longer
41	/// the only way in. What has NOT changed is the rule above: whichever
42	/// container is open, a candidate may not intersect a nest IN it.
43	///
44	/// **A TRANSITION is a wall too** (road map 5's E1): an overlap on any
45	/// unlocked track is subtracted from every run, widened by its own length
46	/// each side, so no cut can leave one clip's tail sitting wholly under its
47	/// neighbour. `SilenceDetector+Walls.overlapWalls` is that list and argues
48	/// the widening; unlike a nest it is not REPORTED, because a transition is
49	/// something the person made and expects to survive rather than something
50	/// the sheet owes them an explanation for.
51	///
52	/// Nothing here is AppKit, a view or a document beyond one read: `Input.read`
53	/// is the seam that takes a snapshot, a plan, a selection and the peak files
54	/// off a `ProjectDocument` once, and everything after it is arithmetic over
55	/// values. That is what lets the sheet recompute synchronously on every
56	/// control change and lets the agent's `detect_silence` run the same code.
57	///
58	/// The units, once, because three of them are easy to confuse:
59	/// * a **bucket** is 1/100 s of SOURCE time — exactly
60	///   `ReelTime.perSecond / MediaImporter.peakBucketsPerSecond` ticks;
61	/// * a **segment** maps project time to source time at the speed the plan
62	///   already resolved (`duration / sourceDuration`);
63	/// * a **span** this answers with is PROJECT time, snapped to the frame grid.
64	///
65	/// The first two of those, and the reversed mirror they need, are
66	/// `MediaPeaks`' since road map 2 phase 5c: Normalise Clip asks the cache the
67	/// same question this does, and a second copy of the arithmetic would have
68	/// been the third project-to-source conversion in the app. **The envelope
69	/// followed them**, once phase 5's level meter had written its own copy of the
70	/// piecewise-linear ramp search: `MediaPeaks.envelope` is the app's one
71	/// spelling of the mix rule and this file is one of its two readers. Nothing
72	/// about the numbers changed when either moved.
73	enum SilenceDetector {
74	
75	    // MARK: - Input
76	
77	    /// One audio segment with everything the quiet test needs beside it.
78	    /// Built once per `Input`, because none of it depends on the settings.
79	    fileprivate struct Voice {
80	        let segment: PlanSegment
81	        /// The envelope of the composition track this segment plays on.
82	        let ramps: [PlanRamp]?
83	        /// The forward file's buckets, or nil when the cache is not on disk.
84	        let peaks: [Float]?
85	        /// The media's model duration when the clip plays BACKWARDS, which is
86	        /// the pivot `ReverseRenderer` mirrors about; nil otherwise.
87	        /// `MediaPeaks.reversedPivot` works it out and says why it cannot be
88	        /// read off the plan.
89	        let reversedPivot: Ticks?
90	        /// True when the track envelope is not identically zero over the
91	        /// segment. It is BOTH scopes' membership test, not just its
92	        /// namesake's — `detect` says why a silenced voice cannot be scoped.
93	        let audible: Bool
94	        /// The forward file's cached Silero VAD probabilities, or nil when
95	        /// the cache is not on disk — road map 4's voice mode.
96	        let speech: [Float]?
97	
98	        var end: Ticks { segment.start + max(0, segment.duration) }
99	    }
100	
101	    /// One nest clip a cut must not land inside, and its id so the sheet can
102	    /// name what it left alone.
103	    ///
104	    /// A nest on a LOCKED track is not one of these: `clear_range` neither
105	    /// splits nor removes there and `shift_clips` does not move it either,
106	    /// so nothing of it can be lost. Built once per `Input`, like `Voice`
107	    /// and for the same reason — it is a function of the snapshot alone.
108	    struct NestExtent {
109	        let clip: UInt32
110	        let span: Span
111	    }
112	
113	    /// Everything a detection run reads, taken off the document ONCE.
114	    ///
115	    /// The document cannot change while a sheet is attached (every editor
116	    /// action validates false then), so the sheet builds one of these when it
117	    /// opens and recomputes from it on every control change without touching
118	    /// the document again. The agent's handler builds one per call.
119	    struct Input {
120	        let snapshot: ProjectSnapshot
121	        let selection: Set<UInt32>
122	        /// Every media in the timeline whose peaks are still missing, whether
123	        /// or not it is in scope — what the sheet names as "still analysing".
124	        let pendingMedia: [UInt32]
125	        /// `SileroVAD.isAvailable`, read once here so `detect` (pure and
126	        /// synchronous) never asks the model directly.
127	        let voiceAvailable: Bool
128	        /// Every media in the timeline whose `cache/speech/<id>.bin` is not
129	        /// on disk yet, whether or not it is in scope — `pendingMedia`'s
130	        /// shape for the voice cache. `MediaSpeech.loader`'s `pending`, sorted.
131	        let pendingSpeech: [UInt32]
132	        fileprivate let voices: [Voice]
133	        /// The spans no candidate may reach into — see `NestExtent`.
134	        fileprivate let nests: [NestExtent]
135	        /// The spans around every OVERLAP on every unlocked track, widened
136	        /// by the overlap's own length each side
137	        /// (`SilenceDetector+Walls.overlapWalls`). Subtracted exactly as the
138	        /// nest walls are and never REPORTED: a nest a cut was kept out of
139	        /// is something to explain, where a transition is a thing the person
140	        /// made on purpose and expects to survive.
141	        fileprivate let walls: [Span]
142	
143	        /// False when the plan has no audio at all, which is the one case
144	        /// worth refusing the sheet outright for.
145	        var hasAudio: Bool { !voices.isEmpty }
146	
147	        /// The scope to open with: the selection when it holds anything
148	        /// AUDIBLE, else everything audible. A selection of picture-only
149	        /// clips would otherwise open a sheet that can only say "nothing to
150	        /// analyse" — and a selection of MUTED ones has to answer `.audible`
151	        /// for the same reason the scope itself drops them: a silenced voice
152	        /// covers its span while reading quiet at every tick, so opening on
153	        /// it would propose cutting the whole clip, and everything under it,
154	        /// away. `SilenceSheetController` disables the "Selected clips" row
155	        /// off exactly this answer.
156	        var defaultScope: Scope {
157	            voices.contains { $0.audible && selection.contains($0.segment.clip) }
158	                ? .selected : .audible
159	        }
160	    }
161	
162	    /// Reads a document's snapshot, plan, selection and peak caches.
163	    ///
164	    /// `selection` overrides the document's own, which is what the agent's
165	    /// `detect_silence {clips}` argument needs; the sheet passes nil.
166	    /// nil is answered only when the core emitted a plan this build cannot
167	    /// read — the same failure `CompositionBuilder` treats as fatal.
168	    static func read(from document: ProjectDocument, selection: Set<UInt32>? = nil) -> Input? {
169	        // The EDITED project (road map 2's phase 9): with a nest open the
170	        // scope, the plan and the ranges `ripple_delete_ranges` is sent are
171	        // all the NEST's, in the nest's own time, and the op carries the
172	        // scope. At the top level this is `document.project` as before.
173	        guard let plan = document.editedProject.plan else { return nil }
174	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
175	        let cacheDirectory = document.cacheDirectory
176	
177	        // One read per media, however many segments cite it — `MediaPeaks.loader`
178	        // (a `MediaCacheLoader`) is that memo, and its `pending` set is what
179	        // this reports as "still analysing".
180	        let loader = MediaPeaks.loader(cacheDirectory: cacheDirectory)
181	        // One read per media, exactly `loader`'s shape, for the voice cache.
182	        let speechLoader = MediaSpeech.loader(cacheDirectory: cacheDirectory)
183	
184	        var voices: [Voice] = []
185	        for track in plan.audioTracks {
186	            for segment in track.segments where segment.duration > 0 {
187	                let span = (segment.start, segment.start + segment.duration)
188	                voices.append(
189	                    Voice(
190	                        segment: segment, ramps: track.ramps,
191	                        peaks: loader.value(for: segment.media),
192	                        reversedPivot: MediaPeaks.reversedPivot(for: segment, in: snapshot),
193	                        audible: isAudible(track.ramps, over: span),
194	                        speech: speechLoader.value(for: segment.media)))
195	            }
196	        }
197	        let nests = nestExtents(in: snapshot)
198	        return Input(
199	            snapshot: snapshot, selection: selection ?? document.selection,
200	            pendingMedia: loader.pending.sorted(), voiceAvailable: SileroVAD.isAvailable,
201	            pendingSpeech: speechLoader.pending.sorted(), voices: voices, nests: nests,
202	            walls: overlapWalls(snapshot))
203	    }
204	
205	    // MARK: - Detection
206	
207	    /// The quiet spans, in project ticks, snapped to the frame grid.
208	    ///
209	    /// The walk is over PROJECT time in bucket-sized steps, so the resolution
210	    /// is one bucket (10 ms) however fast or slow a clip is playing. Within
211	    /// one step a segment's loudness is the MAX over every bucket the step
212	    /// covers, which is the conservative reading for a destructive edit: a
213	    /// clip at ×2 covers two buckets per step and taking the louder of them
214	    /// can only keep material, never cut more.
215	    ///
216	    /// A tick covered by NO segment in scope is not a candidate. "Remove
217	    /// Silences" means "take the dead air out of my recording", not "close
218	    /// every gap in my edit" — a hole between a title card and the footage is
219	    /// deliberate spacing and shading it would promise a cut nobody asked for.
220	    static func detect(_ input: Input, settings: Settings) -> Outcome {
221	        // `audible` is asked of BOTH scopes, not only of its namesake. A
222	        // voice the mix has silenced — muted, silenced by another track's
223	        // solo, turned down, faded to nothing — reads as quiet at every tick
224	        // by construction, because `level` short-circuits on a zero envelope.
225	        // In scope it would therefore COVER its whole span while never
226	        // failing the quiet test, and a selected muted music bed would
227	        // propose one cut across the entire song, taking the audible
228	        // voiceover under it with the ripple. Dropping it keeps the reading
229	        // this file is built on — a silenced clip does not BLOCK a cut — and
230	        // leaves a span nothing audible covers a hole, which is never a
231	        // candidate.
232	        let scoped = input.voices.filter { voice in
233	            guard voice.audible else { return false }
234	            switch settings.scope {
235	            case .selected: return input.selection.contains(voice.segment.clip)
236	            case .audible: return true
237	            }
238	        }
239	        let clips = Set(scoped.map { $0.segment.clip }).sorted()
240	        let pending = Set(scoped.filter { $0.peaks == nil }.map { $0.segment.media }).sorted()
241	        guard !scoped.isEmpty else {
242	            return Outcome(
243	                spans: [], scope: settings.scope, clips: [], pendingMedia: [],
244	                protectedNests: [], mode: settings.mode, judgedByLevel: [], voicePending: [],
245	                proposedMedia: [], answers: [])
246	        }
247	
248	        // Road map 4's voice mode, judged PER VOICE: a window holding no
249	        // voice falls back to level for its whole span and names its media
250	        // (and, through `answers`, its clip), mixed or not; a pending cache
251	        // is never quiet by the model. Both sets stay empty in `.level` mode.
252	        var judgedByLevelMedia: Set<UInt32> = []
253	        var voicePendingMedia: Set<UInt32> = []
254	        let judged: [(voice: Voice, byLevel: Bool)] = scoped.map { voice in
255	            guard settings.mode == .voice else { return (voice, false) }
256	            guard let speech = voice.speech else {
257	                voicePendingMedia.insert(voice.segment.media)
258	                return (voice, false)
259	            }
260	            let whole = Double(
261	                MediaSpeech.speechMax(
262	                    speech, over: voice.segment, from: voice.segment.start, to: voice.end,
263	                    reversedPivot: voice.reversedPivot))
264	            guard whole < settings.voiceConfidence else { return (voice, false) }
265	            judgedByLevelMedia.insert(voice.segment.media)
266	            return (voice, true)
267	        }
268	
269	        let step = MediaPeaks.bucketTicks
270	        let limit = Double(AudioDSP.gain(fromDecibels: Float(settings.thresholdDB)))
271	        let ordered = judged.sorted { $0.voice.segment.start < $1.voice.segment.start }
272	        let domainStart = max(0, ordered.map { $0.voice.segment.start }.min() ?? 0)
273	        let domainEnd = ordered.map { $0.voice.end }.max() ?? domainStart
274	
275	        // The walk is aligned to absolute multiples of a bucket rather than to
276	        // the first segment, so two projects that differ only in where their
277	        // audio starts round the same way.
278	        var t = (domainStart / step) * step
279	        var next = 0
280	        var active: [(voice: Voice, byLevel: Bool)] = []
281	        var runStart: Ticks?
282	        var runs: [Span] = []
283	        while t < domainEnd {
284	            let slotEnd = t + step
285	            while next < ordered.count, ordered[next].voice.segment.start < slotEnd {
286	                active.append(ordered[next])
287	                next += 1
288	            }
289	            active.removeAll { $0.voice.end <= t }
290	
291	            var covered = false
292	            var quiet = true
293	            for entry in active {
294	                let from = max(t, entry.voice.segment.start)
295	                let to = min(slotEnd, entry.voice.end)
296	                guard to > from else { continue }
297	                covered = true
298	                if !isQuiet(
299	                    entry.voice, from: from, to: to, limit: limit, mode: settings.mode,
300	                    voiceConfidence: settings.voiceConfidence, byLevel: entry.byLevel) {
301	                    quiet = false
302	                    break
303	                }
304	            }
305	
306	            if covered && quiet {
307	                if runStart == nil { runStart = max(t, domainStart) }
308	            } else if let start = runStart {
309	                runs.append(Span(start: start, end: min(t, domainEnd)))
310	                runStart = nil
311	            }
312	            t = slotEnd
313	        }
314	        if let start = runStart, domainEnd > start {
315	            runs.append(Span(start: start, end: domainEnd))
316	        }
317	
318	        // The walls go in BEFORE the minimum length, not after: cutting a
319	        // run against a nest first is what turns a run whose middle is a
320	        // nest into two SHORT pieces the minimum then drops, where filtering
321	        // first would leave one long candidate spanning the nest.
322	        let (outside, walled) = excludingNests(
323	            runs, input.nests, minLength: settings.minLength)
324	        // The transition walls, subtracted on the same terms and in the same
325	        // place — before the minimum length, for the reason above — but
326	        // never REPORTED: `excludingNests`' second answer is the sheet's
327	        // list of protected NESTS, and an overlap is not one.
328	        let clear =
329	            input.walls.isEmpty
330	            ? outside
331	            : excludingNests(
332	                outside, input.walls.map { NestExtent(clip: 0, span: $0) },
333	                minLength: settings.minLength
334	            ).0
335	        let spans = refine(clear, settings: settings, fps: input.snapshot.canvas.fps)
336	        // Which media the answer proposes a span INSIDE — `Outcome.proposedMedia`
337	        // says why the two notes need it.
338	        let proposed = Set(
339	            scoped.filter { voice in
340	                spans.contains { $0.start < voice.end && voice.segment.start < $0.end }
341	            }.map { $0.segment.media })
342	        // And each voice's OWN answer (#107): its own overlap test, never
343	        // the media's membership above, so of two clips of one file only the
344	        // one a span lands inside is proposed. `waiting` is the cache
345	        // `isQuiet` reads after the floor.
346	        let answers = judged.map { entry -> VoiceAnswer in
347	            let voice = entry.voice
348	            let inside = spans.contains { $0.start < voice.end && voice.segment.start < $0.end }
349	            let waiting =
350	                settings.mode == .level || entry.byLevel
351	                ? voice.peaks == nil : voice.speech == nil
352	            return VoiceAnswer(
353	                clip: voice.segment.clip, media: voice.segment.media,
354	                span: Span(start: voice.segment.start, end: voice.end),
355	                judgedByLevel: entry.byLevel, waiting: waiting, proposed: inside)
356	        }.sorted { ($0.span.start, $0.clip) < ($1.span.start, $1.clip) }
357	        return Outcome(
358	            spans: spans,
359	            scope: settings.scope, clips: clips, pendingMedia: pending,
360	            protectedNests: walled, mode: settings.mode,
361	            judgedByLevel: judgedByLevelMedia.sorted(), voicePending: voicePendingMedia.sorted(),
362	            proposedMedia: proposed.sorted(), answers: answers)
363	    }
364	
365	    // MARK: - The quiet test
366	
367	    /// The mix envelope at a step, the LOUDER of its two ends — a step that
368	    /// straddles a fade's edge is judged by the loud side. Factored out of
369	    /// `level` for road map 4's floor: a step whose envelope alone lands the
370	    /// quiet threshold at or under full scale is quiet whatever the file
371	    /// holds, in either mode, before either test below is asked.
372	    private static func gain(of voice: Voice, from: Ticks, to: Ticks) -> Double {
373	        max(
374	            MediaPeaks.envelope(voice.ramps, at: from),
375	            MediaPeaks.envelope(voice.ramps, at: max(from, to - 1)))
376	    }
377	
378	    /// `peak × envelope` for one segment over one step of project time — the
379	    /// LEVEL test, byte-identical to what it always answered. A zero
380	    /// envelope short-circuits: a muted, solo-silenced or fully faded
381	    /// segment is silent in the mix whatever its file holds, which is the
382	    /// whole reason the test is written against the plan.
383	    private static func level(of voice: Voice, from: Ticks, to: Ticks, step: Ticks) -> Double {
384	        let g = gain(of: voice, from: from, to: to)
385	        guard g > 0 else { return 0 }
386	        // No peaks on disk yet: never quiet. Treating a missing cache as
387	        // silence would propose deleting the whole clip, which is the one
388	        // failure this feature must not have.
389	        guard let peaks = voice.peaks else { return .infinity }
390	        let magnitude = MediaPeaks.peak(
391	            peaks, over: voice.segment, from: from, to: to, reversedPivot: voice.reversedPivot)
392	        return Double(magnitude) * g
393	    }
394	
395	    /// Whether one voice reads quiet over `[from, to)` — the per-step test
396	    /// the walk asks, in the order road map 4's S1 settled on. `gain <=
397	    /// limit` is the FLOOR: a full-scale sample at that gain lands at or
398	    /// under `thresholdDB`, so a turned-down, faded or ducked voice never
399	    /// holds a cut up, in EITHER mode, before the model is ever consulted —
400	    /// the mix promise the sheet's hint and the tool's catalog entry both
401	    /// make. `byLevel` (this VOICE's source window holds no voice, computed
402	    /// once per voice over its whole segment) and `.level` mode both fall
403	    /// through to the level test unchanged; otherwise a pending cache is
404	    /// never quiet, and the model's answer is the MAX Silero probability
405	    /// over the step, never the mean.
406	    private static func isQuiet(
407	        _ voice: Voice, from: Ticks, to: Ticks, limit: Double, mode: Mode, voiceConfidence: Double,
408	        byLevel: Bool
409	    ) -> Bool {
410	        let g = gain(of: voice, from: from, to: to)
411	        guard g > limit else { return true }
412	        if mode == .level || byLevel {
413	            return level(of: voice, from: from, to: to, step: 0) <= limit
414	        }
415	        guard let speech = voice.speech else { return false }
416	        return Double(
417	            MediaSpeech.speechMax(
418	                speech, over: voice.segment, from: from, to: to,
419	                reversedPivot: voice.reversedPivot)) < voiceConfidence
420	    }
421	
422	    /// Whether a track's envelope is anything but zero across a span. The
423	    /// ramps cover a track's whole extent with no gaps, so a span nothing
424	    /// covers is a plan this build does not understand — believe the segment
425	    /// rather than silence it.
426	    static func isAudible(_ ramps: [PlanRamp]?, over span: (Ticks, Ticks)) -> Bool {
427	        guard let ramps = ramps, !ramps.isEmpty else { return true }
428	        var covered = false
429	        for ramp in ramps {
430	            let end = ramp.start + max(0, ramp.duration)
431	            guard end > span.0, ramp.start < span.1 else { continue }
432	            covered = true
433	            if max(ramp.from, ramp.to) > 0 { return true }
434	        }
435	        return !covered
436	    }
437	
438	}

3	/// The detector's vocabulary — `Span`, `Scope`, `Mode`, `Settings` and
4	/// `Outcome` — a pure move out of `SilenceDetector.swift`, #107's toll,
5	/// landed first and alone. The file that was to take on per-voice answers
6	/// sat at the cap, and these five types are the piece of it every caller
7	/// names (the sheet, the tool, the timeline's wash, Normalize Clip, the
8	/// recorder's landing, the probes) while none of them reads the walk. None
9	/// of it was `private`, so the cut widened nothing: the types came here
10	/// whole, in their order, with their bodies untouched.
11	extension SilenceDetector {
12	
13	    // MARK: - Vocabulary
14	
15	    /// One quiet span of project time, in ticks. Half-open: `end` is the
16	    /// first tick that is NOT removed, which is what the op's `[from, to]`
17	    /// pair means too.
18	    struct Span: Equatable {
19	        let start: Ticks
20	        let end: Ticks
21	
22	        var length: Ticks { max(0, end - start) }
23	    }
24	
25	    /// Which clips the quiet test is taken over.
26	    ///
27	    /// The rule is an INTERSECTION — a tick is quiet only where every clip in
28	    /// scope is quiet — so the scope is what stops a music bed under a
29	    /// voiceover from being cut away with the pauses in the speech.
30	    enum Scope: String, CaseIterable {
31	        /// The clips the user has selected — their AUDIBLE segments only.
32	        /// A selected clip that plays no sound, or none the mix lets
33	        /// through, simply contributes none (`detect` says why).
34	        case selected
35	        /// Every audio segment whose track envelope is not identically zero
36	        /// across it — i.e. everything actually audible in the mix.
37	        case audible
38	
39	        var displayName: String {
40	            switch self {
41	            case .selected: return "Selected clips"
42	            case .audible: return "All audible clips"
43	            }
44	        }
45	    }
46	
47	    /// How a moment is judged quiet — road map 4's S1. `voice` asks the
48	    /// cached Silero VAD probability (`cache/speech/<id>.bin`) and falls
49	    /// back to `level` per VOICE whose source window holds no voice, or for
50	    /// every media at once when the model cannot be used this process;
51	    /// `level` is today's rule, byte for byte. A media whose speech cache
52	    /// has NOT landed is judged by neither — see `Outcome.voicePending`.
53	    enum Mode: String, CaseIterable {
54	        case voice
55	        case level
56	
57	        var displayName: String {
58	            switch self {
59	            case .voice: return "Voice"
60	            case .level: return "Level"
61	            }
62	        }
63	    }
64	
65	    /// The four numbers the sheet and the `detect_silence` tool both spell.
66	    struct Settings: Equatable {
67	        /// The level, in dBFS, at or under which a moment counts as quiet —
68	        /// measured IN THE MIX (see the type's doc). −40 dBFS is roughly a
69	        /// quiet room's tone under a spoken take: low enough that breath and
70	        /// keyboard noise survive, high enough that a real pause reads as one.
71	        var thresholdDB: Double
72	        /// The shortest quiet run worth cutting. Half a second is about the
73	        /// length of a deliberate pause in speech; anything shorter is the gap
74	        /// between two words and removing it makes the delivery sound clipped.
75	        var minLength: Ticks
76	        /// How much of each end of a quiet run is KEPT, so a cut does not land
77	        /// on the attack of the next word. A tenth of a second is three frames
78	        /// at 30 fps — the smallest amount that reliably reads as breathing
79	        /// room rather than as an edit.
80	        var padding: Ticks
81	        var scope: Scope
82	        /// `voice` by default; the sheet opens in `level` when the model
83	        /// cannot be used this process.
84	        var mode: Mode
85	        /// The Silero probability at or above which a moment counts as
86	        /// speech, in `voice` mode. Read only in that mode — the tool
87	        /// refuses it in `level`, named rather than silently ignored.
88	        var voiceConfidence: Double
89	
90	        static let defaultThresholdDB = -40.0
91	        static let defaultMinLength: Ticks = ReelTime.ticks(seconds: 0.5)
92	        static let defaultPadding: Ticks = ReelTime.ticks(seconds: 0.1)
93	        static let defaultVoiceConfidence = 0.5
94	
95	        /// The ranges the sheet's controls and the tool's arguments clamp to.
96	        /// −80 dBFS is under any real recording's noise floor and −10 dBFS is
97	        /// well into speech, so the two ends are "cut nothing" and "cut
98	        /// almost everything" rather than arbitrary numbers.
99	        static let thresholdRange = -80.0...(-10.0)
100	        static let minLengthRange = 0.05...10.0
101	        static let paddingRange = 0.0...2.0
102	        static let voiceConfidenceRange = 0.1...0.9
103	
104	        init(
105	            thresholdDB: Double = Settings.defaultThresholdDB,
106	            minLength: Ticks = Settings.defaultMinLength,
107	            padding: Ticks = Settings.defaultPadding,
108	            scope: Scope = .audible,
109	            mode: Mode = .voice,
110	            voiceConfidence: Double = Settings.defaultVoiceConfidence
111	        ) {
112	            self.thresholdDB = thresholdDB
113	            self.minLength = minLength
114	            self.padding = padding
115	            self.scope = scope
116	            self.mode = mode
117	            self.voiceConfidence = voiceConfidence
118	        }
119	    }
120	
121	    /// What one detection run found.
122	    struct Outcome {
123	        let spans: [Span]
124	        /// The scope the run actually used — the sheet SAYS which, because
125	        /// "nothing was found" and "nothing was looked at" are different
126	        /// answers and the user cannot tell them apart otherwise.
127	        let scope: Scope
128	        /// Distinct clip ids that contributed a segment, sorted.
129	        let clips: [UInt32]
130	        /// Media in scope whose `cache/peaks/<id>.bin` has not been written
131	        /// yet. Their segments are treated as NEVER quiet, so a project opened
132	        /// a second ago proposes no cuts rather than proposing to delete a
133	        /// whole clip because its waveform has not landed.
134	        let pendingMedia: [UInt32]
135	        /// Nest clips that held quiet the detector declined to propose, so
136	        /// the sheet can say why it found fewer cuts than the timeline
137	        /// looks like it holds. Empty is the ordinary answer.
138	        let protectedNests: [UInt32]
139	        /// The mode the run actually used — `settings.mode`, echoed back for
140	        /// the same reason `scope` is.
141	        let mode: Mode
142	        /// Distinct media, in scope, with at least one scoped voice whose
143	        /// source window holds no voice and was therefore judged by level
144	        /// even in `voice` mode. Always `[]` in `level` mode. Which CLIPS
145	        /// were is `answers`' (`judgedByLevelClips`).
146	        let judgedByLevel: [UInt32]
147	        /// Distinct media, in scope, whose `cache/speech/<id>.bin` has not
148	        /// landed yet — never quiet by the model, and not judged by level
149	        /// either: a missing cache must not read as silence. Always `[]` in
150	        /// `level` mode.
151	        let voicePending: [UInt32]
152	        /// Distinct media a span in `spans` actually lands inside, sorted.
153	        /// It is what the sheet and the tool make their "nothing inside is
154	        /// proposed" promise about while a cache is still landing: the gain
155	        /// FLOOR is asked before either cache (`isQuiet`), so a clip the mix
156	        /// has turned down, faded or ducked is quiet with nothing on disk at
157	        /// all, and the promise used to deny the ranges printed beside it
158	        /// (the reader review, road map 4 §8, R3·1).
159	        let proposedMedia: [UInt32]
160	        /// One answer per scoped voice, sorted by start and then clip; `[]`
161	        /// when nothing was in scope. The media sets above cannot tell two
162	        /// clips of one file apart — one ducked, one not — so the notes name
163	        /// the CLIP from these (#107).
164	        let answers: [VoiceAnswer]
165	
166	        var removed: Ticks { spans.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.length } }
167	        var isEmpty: Bool { spans.isEmpty }
168	    }
169	
170	    /// One scoped voice's own answer (#107): which clip, over which span,
171	    /// judged how, and whether the answer proposes anything inside it.
172	    struct VoiceAnswer: Equatable {
173	        /// `PlanSegment.clip`. Under a nest that is the INNER clip's id,
174	        /// which `snapshot.clip` cannot find — `label(in:)` falls back.
175	        let clip: UInt32
176	        let media: UInt32
177	        /// The segment's project span, `[start, start + duration)`.
178	        let span: Span
179	        /// Its source window holds no voice, so it was judged by level.
180	        let judgedByLevel: Bool
181	        /// The cache the quiet test reads after the gain floor has not
182	        /// landed: the waveform in `level` mode or for a by-level voice,
183	        /// else the speech cache. A waiting voice is quiet by the FLOOR or
184	        /// not at all, so one that is also `proposed` is quiet by the mix.
185	        let waiting: Bool
186	        /// A span in `Outcome.spans` overlaps this voice's own span.
187	        let proposed: Bool
188	
189	        /// "<clip name> at <timecode>", the sheet's name for a clip — the
190	        /// media's name, then "clip <id>", when the snapshot cannot find it.
191	        func label(in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> String {
192	            let name = snapshot.clip(clip).map { snapshot.name(of: $0) }
193	                ?? snapshot.media(media)?.name ?? "clip \(clip)"
194	            return "\(name) at "
195	                + ReelTime.format(span.start, fps: snapshot.canvas.fps, frames: true)
196	        }
197	
198	        /// One label per distinct clip and start, in the order given.
199	        static func labels(_ answers: [VoiceAnswer], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> [String] {
200	            var seen: [(UInt32, Ticks)] = []
201	            var labels: [String] = []
202	            for answer in answers {
203	                let key = (answer.clip, answer.span.start)
204	                guard !seen.contains(where: { $0 == key }) else { continue }
205	                seen.append(key)
206	                labels.append(answer.label(in: snapshot))
207	            }
208	            return labels
209	        }
210	    }
211	}

3	/// The nest walls and the frame-grid snap: a pure move out of
4	/// `SilenceDetector.swift`, road map 4's toll 1, landed first and alone. The
5	/// file that took on the voice model needed the room, and these five
6	/// functions plus `NestExtent` are the piece of the detector that answers
7	/// only to the SNAPSHOT — no plan, no peaks, no model — so the cut cost
8	/// nothing but visibility: `excludingNests`, `overlap`, `merged`,
9	/// `snapUpToFrame` and `snapDownToFrame` widen `private` to internal, since
10	/// an extension member in another file cannot see another file's `private`.
11	///
12	/// `refine` came the same way and for the same reason, as road map 4's toll
13	/// for the reader review's fixes: it is the third thing here that answers to
14	/// the SNAPSHOT alone (a run, the two lengths and the frame grid), it calls
15	/// both snaps, and it widens to internal beside them.
16	extension SilenceDetector {
17	
18	    // MARK: - The walls
19	
20	    /// The nest walls of a snapshot. Top-level clips only, which is exactly
21	    /// right: a nest INSIDE a nest is already behind the outer one's wall,
22	    /// and the op can only ever split what `Project::clip` can name.
23	    static func nestExtents(in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> [NestExtent] {
24	        snapshot.clips.compactMap { clip in
25	            guard case .nest = clip.source, clip.duration > 0,
26	                  // A track this build cannot find is treated as unlocked:
27	                  // the conservative reading, since being wrong the other
28	                  // way is the one that loses material.
29	                  snapshot.track(clip.track)?.locked != true
30	            else { return nil }
31	            return NestExtent(
32	                clip: clip.id, span: Span(start: clip.start, end: clip.start + clip.duration))
33	        }
34	    }
35	
36	    /// Every run cut into the pieces that lie OUTSIDE every nest clip, with
37	    /// the nests that took a cut's worth of quiet away named alongside.
38	    ///
39	    /// A piece may end exactly where a nest begins, and that is safe:
40	    /// `clear_range` cuts its bounds with `split_under_playhead`, which
41	    /// splits only what a tick falls STRICTLY inside, so a bound on a nest
42	    /// clip's own edge splits nothing and the ripple then moves the whole
43	    /// nest clip left — a move, not a cut into it. Nor can the op weld two
44	    /// pieces back together across a nest: it merges spans that overlap or
45	    /// TOUCH, and these are a nest clip's whole length apart.
46	    ///
47	    /// The second answer is the sheet's, and it names a nest only when the
48	    /// quiet inside it was long enough to have BEEN a cut — a stray bucket
49	    /// of room tone behind a wall is not something to explain.
50	    static func excludingNests(
51	        _ runs: [Span], _ nests: [NestExtent], minLength: Ticks
52	    ) -> ([Span], [UInt32]) {
53	        guard !nests.isEmpty else { return (runs, []) }
54	        var walled: Set<UInt32> = []
55	        for nest in nests {
56	            for run in runs where overlap(run, nest.span) >= max(1, minLength) {
57	                walled.insert(nest.clip)
58	            }
59	        }
60	        // Merged first, so two nest clips that abut do not leave a
61	        // zero-length piece between them.
62	        let walls = merged(nests.map { $0.span })
63	        var out: [Span] = []
64	        for run in runs {
65	            var start = run.start
66	            for wall in walls {
67	                if wall.end <= start { continue }
68	                if wall.start >= run.end { break }
69	                if wall.start > start { out.append(Span(start: start, end: wall.start)) }
70	                start = wall.end
71	                if start >= run.end { break }
72	            }
73	            if start < run.end { out.append(Span(start: start, end: run.end)) }
74	        }
75	        return (out, walled.sorted())
76	    }
77	
78	    /// The span around every OVERLAP on every unlocked track — the material
79	    /// a candidate may not reach into, or the transition is destroyed
80	    /// (road map 5, E1).
81	    ///
82	    /// **Every unlocked track, not the detector's scope**, because
83	    /// `ripple_delete_ranges` cuts every unlocked track: a cut proposed from
84	    /// the voice on track 3 shifts the pair on track 1 too, and the nest
85	    /// walls are built the same way for the same reason.
86	    ///
87	    /// **A wall is the overlap WIDENED by its own length on each side** —
88	    /// `[B.start − ov, A.end + ov]` with `ov = A.end − B.start` — snapped
89	    /// OUTWARD to the frame grid, and that is where it differs from a nest
90	    /// wall, which can be exact. A nest clip's edges are places a cut splits
91	    /// nothing; an overlap's edges lie strictly INSIDE the other clip, so an
92	    /// exact wall is not enough. A quiet run ending exactly at `B.start`
93	    /// survives a wall of exactly `[B.start, A.end]`; `clear_range` then
94	    /// splits A at `B.start` and the shift moves A's `ov`-long tail and B
95	    /// together, leaving that tail wholly underneath B — an overlap longer
96	    /// than half the shorter clip, which neither `ripple_delete_ranges` nor
97	    /// `validate` checks. Widened, the nearest legal cut leaves each clip at
98	    /// least `2·ov` across the overlap, which is exactly the half rule's own
99	    /// bound.
100	    ///
101	    /// The transition's `audio` flag is deliberately NOT consulted. The
102	    /// cases that matter are not about the crossfade making the overlap
103	    /// quiet — `max(cos, sin) ≥ 0.707`, so a two-voice overlap is never
104	    /// quiet from the fade alone — but about a pair where only one clip has
105	    /// sound, and about handles pulled out of material Remove Silences had
106	    /// already judged quiet, which is the common case since that is where a
107	    /// person adds a transition after cutting. Neither depends on the flag.
108	    static func overlapWalls(_ snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> [Span] {
109	        var walls: [Span] = []
110	        let fps = snapshot.canvas.fps
111	        for track in snapshot.tracks where !track.locked {
112	            let ordered = snapshot.clips(onTrack: track.id)
113	            for (earlier, later) in zip(ordered, ordered.dropFirst()) {
114	                let start = max(earlier.start, later.start)
115	                let end = min(earlier.end, later.end)
116	                let width = end - start
117	                guard width > 0 else { continue }
118	                walls.append(
119	                    Span(
120	                        start: snapDownToFrame(max(0, start - width), fps: fps),
121	                        end: snapUpToFrame(end + width, fps: fps)))
122	            }
123	        }
124	        return walls
125	    }
126	
127	    /// The length two spans share, or 0.
128	    static func overlap(_ a: Span, _ b: Span) -> Ticks {
129	        max(0, min(a.end, b.end) - max(a.start, b.start))
130	    }
131	
132	    /// Overlapping and touching spans folded together, in start order — the
133	    /// same rule `edit_time.rs`'s `union` applies to the ranges the op is
134	    /// finally handed.
135	    static func merged(_ spans: [Span]) -> [Span] {
136	        var out: [Span] = []
137	        for span in spans.sorted(by: { $0.start < $1.start }) where span.end > span.start {
138	            guard let last = out.last, span.start <= last.end else {
139	                out.append(span)
140	                continue
141	            }
142	            out[out.count - 1] = Span(start: last.start, end: max(last.end, span.end))
143	        }
144	        return out
145	    }
146	
147	    /// Length filter, then padding, then the frame grid — in that order,
148	    /// because the minimum is about the RUN the ear heard and the padding is
149	    /// about the CUT that replaces it.
150	    ///
151	    /// Both bounds snap INWARD: up for the start, down for the end. Inward is
152	    /// the conservative direction for an edit that deletes material — it can
153	    /// leave a frame of room tone, which is inaudible, where outward would
154	    /// clip the attack of the next word, which is not. A frame at 30 fps is
155	    /// 20 000 ticks against a bucket's 6 000, so nearest-snapping could move a
156	    /// cut by more than the detection resolution, and in the wrong direction
157	    /// half the time.
158	    static func refine(_ runs: [Span], settings: Settings, fps: Fps) -> [Span] {
159	        var out: [Span] = []
160	        for run in runs {
161	            guard run.length >= settings.minLength else { continue }
162	            let padded = Span(
163	                start: run.start + settings.padding, end: run.end - settings.padding)
164	            guard padded.end > padded.start else { continue }
165	            let snapped = Span(
166	                start: snapUpToFrame(padded.start, fps: fps),
167	                end: snapDownToFrame(padded.end, fps: fps))
168	            guard snapped.start >= 0, snapped.end > snapped.start else { continue }
169	            out.append(snapped)
170	        }
171	        return out
172	    }
173	
174	    // MARK: - Frame snapping, directionally
175	
176	    /// The core has `snap_up_to_frame` / `snap_down_to_frame` (the directional
177	    /// pair phase 1 added for exactly this), but neither crosses the FFI —
178	    /// `rc_time_snap_to_frame` is the whole C surface for time. So the two are
179	    /// composed here from the two pieces Swift DOES have, `ReelTime.snapToFrame`
180	    /// and `Fps.frameDuration`, rather than re-deriving a grid: the nearest
181	    /// boundary is asked for, and when it fell the wrong way the neighbouring
182	    /// one is asked for instead.
183	    static func snapUpToFrame(_ t: Ticks, fps: Fps) -> Ticks {
184	        let nearest = ReelTime.snapToFrame(t, fps: fps)
185	        guard nearest < t else { return nearest }
186	        return ReelTime.snapToFrame(nearest + max(fps.frameDuration, 1), fps: fps)
187	    }
188	
189	    static func snapDownToFrame(_ t: Ticks, fps: Fps) -> Ticks {
190	        let nearest = ReelTime.snapToFrame(t, fps: fps)
191	        guard nearest > t else { return nearest }
192	        return ReelTime.snapToFrame(nearest - max(fps.frameDuration, 1), fps: fps)
193	    }
194	}

310	            // waits for the waveform (the reader review, road map 4 §8, R3·1).
311	            notes.append(

365	    private func promise(about pending: [UInt32]) -> String {
366	        let labels = SilenceDetector.VoiceAnswer.labels(
367	            outcome.mixAnswers(inside: Set(pending)), in: input.snapshot)
368	        guard !labels.isEmpty else { return "Nothing inside is proposed for removal yet." }

376	    /// landed for most of what is on screen, so a media whose waveform is
377	    /// late still has spans proposed inside it BY THE MODEL — `promise` would
378	    /// then answer "quiet in the MIX", which is false about a clip nothing

380	    /// the clips of those media whose own answer is proposed while the cache
381	    /// their quiet test reads is missing (`Outcome.mixAnswers`) — a clip that
382	    /// holds no voice waiting on this waveform, or one whose speech cache has
383	    /// not landed either (`SilenceDetector.detect` returns on a missing
384	    /// speech cache BEFORE the by-level test, so such a clip is waiting on
385	    /// its speech). Only the FLOOR can propose inside a waiting clip, so what
386	    /// it names is what the mix made quiet, and a clip of the same file the
387	    /// mix left alone is not named.
388	    private func waveformPromise() -> String {
389	        let plain = "Anything inside it that holds no voice is left alone until it lands"
390	        let labels = SilenceDetector.VoiceAnswer.labels(
391	            outcome.mixAnswers(inside: Set(outcome.pendingMedia)), in: input.snapshot)
392	        guard !labels.isEmpty else { return plain + "." }
393	        return plain + ", except where the mix already turns "
394	            + labels.joined(separator: ", ") + " down far enough to be quiet."
395	    }

404	        // Write the clamped value back, so a number the formatter let through
405	        // but `Settings` bounds does not stay on screen as if it had been
406	        // taken.

412	    /// A peaks or speech file landed, or was WITHDRAWN. Re-read the input —
413	    /// that is the only way to pick the new floats up, since `Input` holds
414	    /// them by value — and recompute.
415	    ///
416	    /// It re-reads whether or not anything is PENDING. It used to stop unless
417	    /// `pendingMedia` or `pendingSpeech` held something, and the post that
418	    /// matters most arrives when neither does: a relink driven from the agent
419	    /// while this sheet is up withdraws the old `.bin` FIRST, so the sheet
420	    /// went on showing spans measured from a file the project no longer uses
421	    /// until something else woke it (the reader review, road map 4 §8, R2·2 —
422	    /// the limit `archive/remaining.md` §5 recorded as unprovable, on
423	    /// the belief that no proof could drive this sheet; `silence2_probe.py`'s
424	    /// claim 17 does). The media id is not checked against the scope: a file
425	    /// this project does not use posts nothing, and a re-read costs one pass
426	    /// over caches that are already in the page cache.
427	    @objc private func cacheChanged(_ note: Notification) {
428	        let kind = note.userInfo?[MediaImporter.cacheKindKey] as? String
429	        guard kind == MediaImporter.peaksKind || kind == MediaImporter.speechKind,
430	              let document = document,
431	              let reread = SilenceDetector.read(from: document)
432	        else { return }
433	        input = reread
434	        refresh()

443	    /// ONE `ripple_delete_ranges` for however many spans — one op, one undo
444	    /// step, and the core's own merge-then-cut-right-to-left rule rather than
445	    /// N ripples sent in a row (which would each shift the ones after it).
446	    ///
447	    /// Nothing is sent when there is nothing to cut: `applyEdit` answers the
448	    /// core's identity with a beep, and a beep at a dialog the user has just
449	    /// confirmed reads as a refusal rather than as "nothing to do". The
450	    /// button is disabled for the same reason, and AppKit skips a disabled
451	    /// button when it looks for the Return key's target, so the guard below
452	    /// should be unreachable — it costs one comparison to be sure.
453	    @objc private func applyClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
454	        // A click on a button does not take the first responder from a text
455	        // field, so a just-typed length has not been committed yet. Ending
456	        // editing runs `controlTextDidEndEditing`, which re-detects; the
457	        // spans are therefore read AFTER it.
458	        guard endSheetFieldEditing() else { return }
459	        let spans = outcome.spans
460	        let document = self.document
461	        dismiss(self)
462	        guard let document = document, !spans.isEmpty else { return }
463	        document.applyEdit(
464	            "Remove Silences",
465	            [.rippleDeleteRanges(ranges: spans.map { (from: $0.start, to: $0.end) })])
466	    }

468	    /// The one teardown point: it fires for Remove, for Cancel, for Escape
469	    /// and for a window closing under the sheet alike. Nothing else clears
470	    /// the wash — the spans are not part of `TimelineView.update(...)`, so
471	    /// leaving them set would paint a permanent tint over a timeline whose
472	    /// clips have since moved.
473	    override func viewDidDisappear() {
474	        super.viewDidDisappear()
475	        editor?.timeline?.candidateSpans = []
476	    }

481	/// The command half, at the foot of the file that owns the feature —

483	/// beside the importer it opens rather than in a file of its own.

485	
486	    /// Clip ▸ Remove Silences… — the body of the frozen file's one-line
487	    /// `@objc func removeSilences(_:)` forward.
488	    ///
489	    /// The detector's input is read HERE rather than in the sheet's `init`,
490	    /// so the two honest refusals happen before a dialog goes up: a plan this
491	    /// build cannot read, and a timeline with no sound in it at all. A sheet
492	    /// whose only possible answer is "nothing to analyse" should not open.
493	    func removeSilencesCommand() {
494	        guard let document = document, view.window?.attachedSheet == nil else {
495	            NSSound.beep()
496	            return
497	        }
498	        guard let input = SilenceDetector.read(from: document), input.hasAudio else {
499	            NSSound.beep()
500	            return
501	        }
502	        // The wash the sheet puts on the lanes is read while it is up, and a
503	        // running playhead repaints over it several times a second.
504	        playback.pause()
505	        presentAsSheet(SilenceSheetController(document: document, editor: self, input: input))
506	    }

508	    /// The half of `validateUserInterfaceItem` this file owns. nil means "not
509	    /// mine" and leaves the other answers alone.
510	    func validateSilenceAction(_ action: Selector) -> Bool? {
511	        guard let document = document else { return false }
512	        switch action {
513	        case #selector(EditorViewController.removeSilences(_:)):
514	            // The honest test is the PLAN — it is what the detector reads —
515	            // but `ReelProject.plan` decodes JSON on every access and a
516	            // validator runs on every menu open. This is the same question
517	            // asked of the snapshot, which is memoized: it is deliberately
518	            // the body of `TimelineView.hasAudio`, and it is copied rather
519	            // than shared because that one lives on a VIEW and a controller
520	            // reaching into the timeline for a model question is the wrong
521	            // direction. The sheet's own guard is the exact answer.
522	            let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
523	            return snapshot.clips.contains { clip in
524	                guard clip.enabled.audio else { return false }
525	                if case .nest = clip.source { return clip.audio != nil }
526	                return snapshot.media(for: clip)?.hasAudio ?? false
527	            }
528	        default:
529	            return nil
530	        }
531	    }
532	}

3	/// The agent's silence tool: the read half of Remove Silences.
4	///
5	/// `detect_silence` is an APP-STATE tool, not an op — it changes nothing and
6	/// registers no undo step. It exists because the detection is Swift's (the
7	/// waveform peaks the package caches are not in the model, and the core does
8	/// no sample work at all — spec §7), so an agent that could only call
9	/// `ripple_delete_ranges` would have to invent the ranges from nothing. The
10	/// pair is deliberate and mirrors the sheet exactly: `detect_silence` is what
11	/// `SilenceSheetController` shows in its live readout, and
12	/// `ripple_delete_ranges` is what its Remove button sends.
13	///
14	/// It stays on the MAIN thread, and so out of `AgentServer.offMainTools`,
15	/// because that set's criterion is "waits for something the main thread has
16	/// to deliver or must not be doing", not "touches the disk":
17	/// `consolidate_media` copies whole media libraries on main and says why, and
18	/// `import_captions` parses a file on main for the same reason. Reading a few
19	/// hundred KB of `cache/peaks/<id>.bin` and making one arithmetic pass over
20	/// it waits on nothing and has no completion to deliver, and being off main
21	/// would cost an `onMain` hop for every document touch — which is where the
22	/// real bugs in this file's neighbours have been.
23	extension AgentServer {
24	
25	    /// The longest a duration argument may be, `snappedTick`'s own ±9.0e15:
26	    /// past it `refine`'s `run.start + padding` overflows. Finding 1 above.
27	    /// Not private: `AgentCatalog+Audio` PUBLISHES it as both durations'
28	    /// `maximum`, so the bound a caller reads and the bound the handler
29	    /// enforces are one number (the second sceptic pass, road map 4 §8).
30	    static let durationCeiling = 9_000_000_000_000_000
31	
32	    /// `detect_silence` — Clip ▸ Remove Silences…
33	    /// (`SilenceSheetController`, whose four controls are these four
34	    /// arguments and whose live "N cuts · removes M:SS" line is this
35	    /// result). Nothing is edited: feed `ranges` to `ripple_delete_ranges`
36	    /// to make the cut, which is what that sheet's button does. The
37	    /// `protected_nests` note is the tool's spelling of the sheet's nest note.
38	    ///
39	    /// Quiet is measured IN THE MIX — the peak bucket times the plan's audio
40	    /// envelope at that tick — so a clip turned down, faded, ducked, muted or
41	    /// silenced by another track's solo is quiet here exactly as it is in the
42	    /// speakers. A tick no clip in scope covers is not a candidate at all: a
43	    /// hole in the timeline is not dead air to be removed.
44	    func detectSilence(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
45	        let document = try target(a)
46	        let clips = try optionalClipsArg(a, "clips", document)
47	        // `clips` is the sheet's scope popup, spelled as the thing an agent
48	        // actually has: ids. Naming any runs the popup's "Selected clips"
49	        // over exactly those — `read` takes a selection override for this
50	        // very reason — and omitting the key takes the sheet's own opening
51	        // rule, which is the document's selection when it holds anything
52	        // with sound and everything audible otherwise. The result reports
53	        // which of the two answered, because "nothing was found" and
54	        // "nothing was looked at" are different answers and no caller can
55	        // tell them apart from an empty list.
56	        guard let input = SilenceDetector.read(from: document, selection: clips.map { Set($0) })
57	        else {
58	            throw ToolError(
59	                message: "The project's audio plan could not be read, so there is nothing to "
60	                    + "measure silence against.")
61	        }
62	        let (settings, modeNote) = try silenceSettings(
63	            a, scope: clips == nil ? input.defaultScope : .selected,
64	            voiceAvailable: input.voiceAvailable)
65	        let outcome = SilenceDetector.detect(input, settings: settings)
66	
67	        var result: [String: Any] = [
68	            "ok": true,
69	            "ranges": outcome.spans.map { [$0.start, $0.end] },
70	            "count": outcome.spans.count,
71	            "removes": outcome.removed,
72	            "scope": outcome.scope.rawValue,
73	            "clips": outcome.clips.map { Int($0) },
74	            "threshold_db": settings.thresholdDB,
75	            "min_length": settings.minLength,
76	            "padding": settings.padding,
77	            "mode": outcome.mode.rawValue,
78	            "voice_confidence": settings.voiceConfidence,
79	            "judged_by_level": outcome.judgedByLevel.map { Int($0) },
80	            // The same answers by CLIP (#107): two clips of one file can be
81	            // judged, and proposed, differently.
82	            "judged_by_level_clips": outcome.judgedByLevelClips.map { Int($0) },
83	        ]
84	        if !outcome.proposedByMixClips.isEmpty {
85	            result["proposed_by_mix_clips"] = outcome.proposedByMixClips.map { Int($0) }
86	        }
87	        var notes: [String] = []
88	        if let modeNote { notes.append(modeNote) }
89	        // Two things worth a sentence rather than a silent zero, because both
90	        // read as "there is no dead air here" and neither is that.
91	        if outcome.clips.isEmpty {
92	            notes.append(
93	                settings.scope == .selected
94	                ? "None of those clips plays any sound, so nothing was analysed."
95	                : "Nothing in this timeline is audible, so nothing was analysed.")
96	        }
97	        // Both waiters fold into ONE key, `pending_peaks` — the union of what
98	        // the level test and the voice test are each still waiting on — so a
99	        // caller that only ever read that key still knows to call again.
100	        let pendingPeaks = Set(outcome.pendingMedia)
101	        let pendingUnion = outcome.mode == .voice
102	            ? pendingPeaks.union(outcome.voicePending) : pendingPeaks
103	        if !pendingUnion.isEmpty {
104	            result["pending_peaks"] = pendingUnion.sorted().map { Int($0) }
105	            // "Nothing inside them is proposed for removal" is a PROMISE about
106	            // the ranges in this same reply, so it is made only about the
107	            // media it holds for. A media with no peaks is never quiet in
108	            // LEVEL mode, so there it holds for every waiter; in VOICE mode a
109	            // media whose waveform is missing but whose speech has landed is
110	            // judged by the model and spans inside it ARE proposed — and the
111	            // sentence used to deny exactly the ranges it was printed beside
112	            // (the reader review, road map 4 §8, R3·1).
113	            let waiter = outcome.mode == .voice ? Set(outcome.voicePending) : pendingPeaks
114	            // And the promise is made about what this ANSWER shows, not about
115	            // the mode: the gain FLOOR is asked before either cache
116	            // (`SilenceDetector.isQuiet`), so a clip the mix has turned down,
117	            // faded, ducked or muted is quiet with nothing on disk at all and
118	            // its spans are right here (the reader review, road map 4 §8,
119	            // finding 2). Whatever the answer proposes inside is dropped from
120	            // the promise, and the clips it is proposed inside are named in
121	            // their own clause (#107).
122	            let proposedInside = waiter.intersection(outcome.proposedMedia)
123	            let blocked = waiter.subtracting(proposedInside)
124	            let waveformOnly = pendingUnion.subtracting(waiter)
125	            var waiting =
126	                "Analysis is still running for \(pendingUnion.count) media file(s); call "
127	                + "again in a moment."
128	            if !blocked.isEmpty {
129	                waiting += blocked.count == pendingUnion.count
130	                    ? " Nothing inside them is proposed for removal."
131	                    : " Nothing inside \(blocked.count) of them is proposed for removal."
132	            }
133	            let mixInside = Self.clipIDs(outcome.mixAnswers(inside: waiter))
134	            if mixInside.count == 1 {
135	                waiting +=
136	                    " Clip \(mixInside[0]) holds spans that ARE proposed here: the mix turns "
137	                    + "it down far enough to be quiet before either cache is asked."
138	            } else if mixInside.count > 1 {
139	                waiting +=
140	                    " Clips \(Self.listed(mixInside)) hold spans that ARE proposed here: the "
141	                    + "mix turns them down far enough to be quiet before either cache is asked."
142	            }
143	            if !waveformOnly.isEmpty {
144	                // The mirror image of the promise above, and it needs the
145	                // same intersection (the reader review's second sceptic pass,
146	                // road map 4 §8). "Spans inside them ARE proposed here" is a
147	                // claim about ranges in this very reply, so a waveform waiter
148	                // the answer proposes NOTHING inside — every clip of it holds
149	                // no voice, so the missing waveform blocks the lot — must not
150	                // be told it has them.
151	                let proposedHere = waveformOnly.intersection(outcome.proposedMedia)
152	                let silentHere = waveformOnly.subtracting(proposedHere)
153	                let ending: String
154	                if silentHere.isEmpty {
155	                    ending = ", so spans inside them ARE proposed here."
156	                } else if proposedHere.isEmpty {
157	                    ending = ", and nothing inside them is proposed here."
158	                } else {
159	                    ending =
160	                        ", so spans inside \(proposedHere.count) of them ARE proposed here "
161	                        + "and nothing inside the other \(silentHere.count) is."
162	                }
163	                waiting +=
164	                    " For \(Self.subject(waveformOnly.count, of: pendingUnion.count)) it is the "
165	                    + "WAVEFORM that has not landed, which in voice mode decides only a clip "
166	                    + "holding no voice" + ending
167	                // And where those spans are the FLOOR's rather than the
168	                // model's, name the clip (#107): a clip that holds no voice
169	                // is proposed without its waveform only because the mix
170	                // already turned it down, and another clip of the same file
171	                // the mix left alone is not. No `voicePending` arm is needed
172	                // here — a voice waiter is in `waiter` above and never in
173	                // `waveformOnly`.
174	                let mixOnly = Self.clipIDs(outcome.mixAnswers(inside: waveformOnly))
175	                if mixOnly.count == 1 {
176	                    waiting +=
177	                        " Clip \(mixOnly[0]) is proposed only where the mix already turns it "
178	                        + "down far enough to be quiet."
179	                } else if mixOnly.count > 1 {
180	                    waiting +=
181	                        " Clips \(Self.listed(mixOnly)) are proposed only where the mix "
182	                        + "already turns them down far enough to be quiet."
183	                }
184	            }
185	            notes.append(waiting)
186	        }
187	        if !outcome.voicePending.isEmpty {
188	            result["voice_pending"] = outcome.voicePending.map { Int($0) }
189	        }
190	        let byLevel = outcome.judgedByLevelClips
191	        if byLevel.count == 1 {
192	            notes.append("Clip \(byLevel[0]) holds no voice and was judged by level.")
193	        } else if byLevel.count > 1 {
194	            notes.append(
195	                "Clips \(Self.listed(byLevel)) hold no voice and were judged by level.")
196	        }
197	        // The sheet's nest note, spelled for an agent (#352): a candidate
198	        // held back at a nest's wall, dropped without a word, reads as "there
199	        // is no dead air here". A listed nest clip is one a quiet run of the
200	        // SCOPED voices crossed (`SilenceDetector+Walls.swift`'s
201	        // `excludingNests`); the nest's own sound is not tested, so it MAY
202	        // hold dead air, and the reader is told to look, not that it does.
203	        // Last, as the sheet puts its nest note last.
204	        if !outcome.protectedNests.isEmpty {
205	            let ids = outcome.protectedNests
206	            result["protected_nests"] = ids.map { Int($0) }
207	            let lead =
208	                ids.count == 1
209	                ? "Quiet that runs across nest clip \(ids[0]) is left alone"
210	                : "Quiet that runs across nest clips \(Self.listed(ids)) is left alone"
211	            let reach =
212	                ids.count == 1
213	                ? "To look for dead air inside it, call set_scope with clip \(ids[0]), then "
214	                    + "detect_silence again."
215	                : "To look for dead air inside them, call set_scope with each clip, then "
216	                    + "detect_silence again."
217	            notes.append(
218	                lead + ": a nest plays from its first frame, so cutting into one would "
219	                    + "strand the rest of it. " + reach)
220	        }
221	        if !notes.isEmpty { result["note"] = notes.joined(separator: " ") }
222	        result["project"] = summary(document)
223	        return try jsonResult(result)
224	    }
225	
226	    /// "that file" / "them" / "2 of them", so a clause about SOME of the
227	    /// waiters never says "the rest" of a sentence that was not printed
228	    /// (the reader review, road map 4 §8, finding 4).
229	    private static func subject(_ count: Int, of total: Int) -> String {
230	        count == total ? (count == 1 ? "that file" : "them") : "\(count) of them"
231	    }
232	
233	    /// The distinct clip ids of some voices' answers, ascending — the tool
234	    /// names a clip by id, as `Transcriber+Jobs` tags one (#107).
235	    private static func clipIDs(_ answers: [SilenceDetector.VoiceAnswer]) -> [UInt32] {
236	        Set(answers.map { $0.clip }).sorted()
237	    }
238	
239	    /// "3, 7, 9".
240	    private static func listed(_ ids: [UInt32]) -> String {
241	        ids.map { String($0) }.joined(separator: ", ")
242	    }
243	
244	    /// The three numbers, read in the sheet's own units and refused by name.
245	    ///
246	    /// The sheet clamps its controls to `Settings`' published ranges because
247	    /// a slider must land somewhere; a tool does not, and clamping an
248	    /// argument silently would report a detection the caller did not ask
249	    /// for. What is refused here is what is not a level or not a length at
250	    /// all — everything else is passed through and named back in the result,
251	    /// so a caller reading `threshold_db` sees what actually ran.
252	    private func silenceSettings(
253	        _ a: [String: Any], scope: SilenceDetector.Scope, voiceAvailable: Bool
254	    ) throws -> (SilenceDetector.Settings, String?) {
255	        var settings = SilenceDetector.Settings(scope: scope)
256	        var note: String?
257	        if let modeString = try stringArg(a, "mode") {
258	            guard let mode = SilenceDetector.Mode(rawValue: modeString) else {
259	                throw ToolError(
260	                    message: "mode must be \"voice\" or \"level\".")
261	            }
262	            if mode == .voice, !voiceAvailable {
263	                throw ToolError(
264	                    message: "The voice model could not be used; call with mode: \"level\".")
265	            }
266	            settings.mode = mode
267	        } else if !voiceAvailable {
268	            settings.mode = .level
269	            note = "The voice model could not be used, so quiet is judged by level."
270	        }
271	        if let voiceConfidence = try doubleArg(a, "voice_confidence") {
272	            guard settings.mode == .voice else {
273	                throw ToolError(
274	                    message: "voice_confidence only applies in mode: \"voice\".")
275	            }
276	            guard voiceConfidence.isFinite,
277	                SilenceDetector.Settings.voiceConfidenceRange.contains(voiceConfidence)
278	            else {
279	                throw ToolError(
280	                    message: "voice_confidence must be a number in "
281	                        + "\(SilenceDetector.Settings.voiceConfidenceRange.lowerBound)…"
282	                        + "\(SilenceDetector.Settings.voiceConfidenceRange.upperBound).")
283	            }
284	            settings.voiceConfidence = voiceConfidence
285	        }
286	        if let thresholdDB = try doubleArg(a, "threshold_db") {
287	            // Above full scale every bucket of every recording counts as
288	            // quiet and the whole timeline comes back as one candidate.
289	            // Peaks are unclamped and a hot source really does read over
290	            // 1.0, so this is a caller's mistake — a level in gain, or a
291	            // sign forgotten — rather than an impossible number.
292	            guard thresholdDB.isFinite, thresholdDB <= 0 else {
293	                throw ToolError(
294	                    message: "threshold_db must be a level at or below 0 dBFS (full scale); "
295	                        + "the default is \(SilenceDetector.Settings.defaultThresholdDB).")
296	            }
297	            settings.thresholdDB = thresholdDB
298	        }
299	        // Both lengths are DURATIONS, and a duration is not a position: they
300	        // are read as given, by the whole-number reader, and are NOT snapped
301	        // to the frame grid. The sheet's own two fields are not snapped
302	        // either (`SilenceSheetController.silenceSettings`'
303	        // `ReelTime.ticks(seconds:)`) and this tool exists to mirror it; the
304	        // frame rule stays where it belongs, on the span BOUNDS `refine`
305	        // produces, so no sub-frame time reaches an op from here. Going
306	        // through `optionalTimeArg` cost that mirror at the DEFAULT rate:
307	        // at 30 fps it ran `padding: 30000` — the sheet's own 0.05 s — as
308	        // 40000, ran `min_length: 45000` as 40000, and dropped
309	        // `padding: 9999` to 0, cutting the material the caller asked to
310	        // keep (the reader review, road map 4 §8, R1·1).
311	        //
312	        // What `optionalTimeArg` DID carry and a duration still needs is its
313	        // CEILING: `refine` adds the padding to a run's start, and a padding
314	        // at `Int64.max` overflowed and killed the app rather than answering
315	        // (the reader review, road map 4 §8, finding 1). The bound is
316	        // `snappedTick`'s own ±9.0e15, refused in a sentence naming the
317	        // argument. The sheet's two fields cannot reach it — they clamp to
318	        // `minLengthRange` and `paddingRange` — so the guard belongs here,
319	        // on the one caller that is not a slider.
320	        if let minLength = try intArg(a, "min_length") {
321	            guard minLength >= 0, minLength <= Self.durationCeiling else {
322	                throw ToolError(
323	                    message: "min_length must be a length in ticks (600000 per second) from 0 "
324	                        + "to \(Self.durationCeiling).")
325	            }
326	            settings.minLength = Ticks(minLength)
327	        }
328	        if let padding = try intArg(a, "padding") {
329	            guard padding >= 0, padding <= Self.durationCeiling else {
330	                throw ToolError(
331	                    message: "padding must be a length in ticks (600000 per second) from 0 "
332	                        + "to \(Self.durationCeiling).")
333	            }
334	            settings.padding = Ticks(padding)
335	        }
336	        return (settings, note)
337	    }
