# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c));
  `PlanSegment.path` (the clip alone when absent) and `origin` (nil) read a nested audio
  segment's instance (spec §11 TX-10); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113); `PlanGate` and
  `gates` a gated clip's hide-while-silent gate (format 43, spec §11 CO-93). `AudioProps.swift`
  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map
  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,
  `hideIdleSteps` and `polished`,
  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and
  `RecipeCursor` (the recipe layer's `cursor`, `media` and `at` required).
  `CutoutProps.swift` (format 39, road map creator-jobs CO2a1, spec §11 CO-20, CO-21;
  `foreground` and the image arm format 41, CO10a, CO-100, CO-101) holds `CutoutSubject`
  (`person`, `foreground`), `CutoutQuality`, `CutoutBackground`, `CutoutProps` (`VideoProps.cutout` and
  `VideoPatch.cutout`; its `dictionary` writes all five keys), `CutoutPatch` (the sparse
  write `VideoPatch.cutoutPart` carries — written under `cutout` only when `cutout` is nil,
  never decoded — so a Background, Edge or Feather row writes its own key alone, CO3),
  `RecipeCutoutMaskKind` (`media`, and `image`, drawn since CO10b from the
  picture's one mask, CO-107),
  `RecipeCutoutMask` (`kind` and `media` required; `subject` lenient,
  `person` when absent, CO-101) and `RecipeCutout` (the recipe layer's
  `cutout`, `mask` required; `subjectCopy`, CO-51); `RecipeLayer.videoProps` passes no cutout — the recipe's is a draw
  instruction, not the clip's props. `VideoProps.swift` (`VideoProps`),
  `ClipSnapshot.swift` (`ClipSource` with its nested `CodingKeys`, `ClipSnapshot`,
  `TransitionSnapshot`) and `TrackSnapshot.swift` (`TrackSnapshot`) are pure moves out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T11–T13). `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no
  agent handler reads a caller-authored OBJECT at all. A scalar enum
  argument is a different thing and several handlers still parse one by name
  (`enumArg` for `add_zoom_action`'s `fit` or an action's `curve`,
  `set_transition`'s `kind` by hand): the
  core refuses those too, and what this rule forbids is decoding a caller's
  object through a lenient type.
  `MotionProps.dictionary` always writes all three keys, `NSNull` for a nil
  slot, because a core patch of `motion` deep-merges — it is the
  APP's writer saying all three slots, not a replace rule, and it is the only
  edge that writes a whole motion. `MotionEdge` also supplies nonpersisted
  zero-duration activity and inactive display/menu titles (E2-27).
  `TextProps.swift` is the text group and `RecipeReveal` (with format version
  9's `textCase` / `words` / `wordStyle`, the recipe's `word` / `wordPop` and,
  since format version 12, `wordGlide` / `wordFill` / `wordDim`), a pure move
  out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift` because a stored property cannot be added
  from an extension. `RecipeReveal` reads and writes its OWN keys — siblings of
  `hash` and `text` in the `text` source — through `init(siblingsOf:)` and
  `encodeSiblings(to:)`, so a new recipe key costs `FrameRecipe.swift`
  nothing; a key spelled other than the snake-case converter spells it
  decodes silently to that key's default (the amount to 1, the rest to nil).
  `ProjectSnapshot+Graphic.swift` mirrors
  `model_graphic.rs`'s `GraphicProps` as `GraphicSnapshot` (`in` is
  `sourceIn`) and `GraphicPropValue` (string, number, bool; anything else
  `.null`), decoded into `ClipSnapshot.graphic`; `props` keys keep the
  module's own spelling (snake-case conversion does not reach a dictionary's
  keys). `WordProps.swift` mirrors `model_words.rs`
  (`TextCase`, `TextWord`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill`, `WordStyle`)
  — `WordStyle.dictionary` writes ALL eight keys (`active_fill` and `pause_dim` since format version 12; `ActivePill.dictionary` writes `glide`), `NSNull` for a nil slot,
  `MotionProps.dictionary`'s rule, because the core deep-merges
  `word_style` — and holds
  what the renderer and the inspector share: `laidContent` (`case` applied —
  every layout and string index is in ITS UTF-16 space, never `content`'s),
  `tokenCount`, `isUntimedPage`, `TextPatch.contentEdit` and
  `InspectorBinding.contentOps` / `ops(textContent:)` — the Content write,
  decided PER CLIP: `words: []` beside the content in one `set_text` only for
  base clips whose count changed, and never `words` in an action end (W-2,
  W-6). It lives there, not in `InspectorPane.swift`, for the size rule.

**The document.**
- `ProjectDocument.swift` (+`DisplayStem`, +`Recording`, +`SelectedAction`, +`Import`, +`Graphics`, +`GraphicFiles`, +`UndoGroup`, +`CacheSaves`, +`Alerts`, +`Reverse`, +`Derived`)
  — NSDocument, `.framejob` package read/write, and the single mutation
  point (see Undo); `applyEdit`'s `.refused` arm beeps and then posts
  `projectDocumentDidRefuse` with the `ReelRefusal` (spec §11 CI-10), which
  the editor forwards to the inspector's refusal strip. Holds the SIX pieces of view state nothing persists —
  playhead, clip selection, in/out range, `selectedMedia`, `nestPath` and
  `selectedAction` — re-clamped by `clampViewState` in that order with the
  scope FIRST, since the selection clamp measures against whatever
  container the scope left. `selectedAction` (spec §11 CI-1) is nil or one
  action of the SINGLE selected clip; `+SelectedAction` holds its queries,
  its one deliberate writer `selectAction(_:)` (which stores nil for an id
  that is not `singleSelectedClip`'s) and the ENTRY rule
  `syncSelectedAction()`, run from `playhead`'s and `selection`'s `didSet`
  against `lastInsideAction`. The clamp re-reads `lastInsideAction` BEFORE
  its last line writes the playhead, so an edit, undo or redo under a
  stationary playhead never enters a span — keep those two lines above
  that write. `nestPath` is a
  PATH of (nest, clip) steps, not a nest id, because two clips can show one
  nest at two starts; `editedProject` is a STORED, memoised `rc_project_scoped`
  handle, and `project` still means the parent for save, export and
  consolidate. A range is cleared on every scope change: a pair of ticks means
  one thing inside a nest and another to an export. `+UndoGroup`:
  `inUndoGroupIfRegistered` runs a body with an undo group pending, and
  `registerUndo(restoring:actionName:)`'s first statement
  (`openPendingUndoGroup()`) opens it at the body's first registration, at the
  body's level and never while undoing or redoing; a body that registers
  nothing leaves undo and redo untouched (#167); `registerUndo` stays the one
  registrar. `applyEdit(_:_:amending:)` (#272) undoes the step that ended at
  `step` before committing, when `project` is still that handle, so a strip's
  off-knob double-click is one step. `cacheDirectory` calls `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` when it
  creates `cache/` — only if the package's date, read through a fresh `URL`
  before the create, is still `fileModificationDate`, so an outside change made before it is not absorbed — and that method re-reads the date through a fresh
  `URL`, because `fileURL` still holds the date it cached at open (#138).
  `+CacheSaves` is the `save(to:ofType:for:completionHandler:)` override
  every save funnels through, bracketing it with the cache ledger's
  `saveBegan` / `saveEnded` (#115, #169).
  `+Import` is File ▸ Add Media… and every drop into an open project
  (`importMedia`, the probe chain and the one grouped commit), the opening
  read's probe (`probeForOpening`, a cancelled copy as `.userCancelled`), and the Media
  tab's Relink… and the missing-media sheet's body (`relinkMedia(_:)`: each
  file probed through `MediaImporter.probe`, one grouped "Relink Media" edit
  carrying each descriptor as `relink_media`'s `probe`, spec §11 #63, then
  `generateCaches()`; the missing-media sheet's door then alerts each
  unreadable file and each refused sentence (#180) through `present(_:)`).
  `+MissingCopies` re-copies, on open, a WebM/MKV copy that is missing or in
  the Trash from its recorded original (spec §11 #228-O), through
  `MediaImporter.probeBuiltInCopy` (never ffmpeg, never a question); a
  read on main or inside `withoutAsking` (an agent's `open_project`, off
  main since #231) passes no watch; and, after the media re-anchor and
  before the re-copy, `reanchoringCursorFiles` re-points a cursor file found
  again at `<package>/media/<same name>` (spec §11 CU-52).
  `+Alerts` is `present(_:)`: every error the document shows waits in one
  queue (`DocumentAlertQueue`) and shows one alert sheet at a time, each asked
  for a main-queue turn after the last one's `didPresent` or the window's last
  sheet end, and only while no sheet is attached, since AppKit drops an error
  sheet asked for while another is attached (#195, `relink_sheet_probe.py`
  A1–A5); with no window, it is app-modal at once. `+Graphics`
  is the document's side of the package's `graphics/`:
  `startGraphicStore()`, run from `makeWindowControllers()` and seeding an
  untitled document's root from `autosavedContentsFileURL/graphics`, and
  `graphicsWrapper()`, the lazy wrapper the save whitelist carries — for a
  SAVED document it reads `<fileURL>/graphics` itself and never asks the
  store, so a nil store can never drop a saved folder; for an untitled one
  it carries the store's root only when `GraphicStore.holdsContent` (an
  entry, file or directory, that is neither hidden nor the manual) says so
  (spec §11 G-14).
  `startGraphicStore()` also installs the document's compiled set in
  `GraphicRegistry` and observes the store's `.graphicsDidChange`, whose
  handler updates the registry and THEN posts `.projectGraphicsDidChange`
  (object: the document) — never `rescan()` there; `stopGraphicStore()`, from
  `close()`, removes the observer, drops the set, stops the store and removes
  BOTH untitled roots — the graphics root (`removeScratchRoot()`) and
  `temporaryCacheDirectory` (`removeTemporaryCacheDirectory()`); the cache
  root goes at close ONLY, never at the first save, because the timeline and
  any pass in flight still hold its path (G-19 (d)). `startGraphicStore()` also observes the document's own
  `.projectDocumentDidChange` and ends with one `reconcileGraphicNames()`;
  `stopGraphicStore()` removes that observer. `+ConvertedThumbnails`:
  `startCaches()`, from `makeWindowControllers()` in place of
  `generateCaches()`, observes the document's own `.projectDocumentDidChange`

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Remove Filler Words' detector (road map "cut-by-transcript" CT-2, spec §11
4	/// TR-4, TR-7, TR-9): a clip's cached cloud filler words as project ranges
5	/// `ripple_delete_ranges` cuts, every edge on the Silero 32 ms grid and then
6	/// on the frame grid.
7	///
8	/// `SilenceDetector`'s shape: `read(from:clips:)` is the one seam that touches
9	/// a document — its snapshot, its selection, its media URLs and the transcript
10	/// cache, read ONCE — and everything after it (`runs`, `gridded`, `placed`,
11	/// `detect`) is arithmetic over values. The words are a Swift cache like the
12	/// peaks (spec §7), so nothing here crosses the FFI.
13	///
14	/// **Only a transcript that asked for fillers is read** (TR-7): the scope's
15	/// files come through `fillersFile`, whose marker must serve `.fillers`
16	/// (TR-2's one rule, `TranscriptStamp.serves`). A media without one is named
17	/// in `needsTranscript` and gives no candidate. The NEIGHBOURS' words — which
18	/// protect a span from a cut — are taken from any transcript that serves
19	/// `.captions`, because a word is a word whichever request heard it.
20	///
21	/// **TR-9, the edges.** A run of consecutive fillers is widened OUTWARD to the
22	/// grid so the whole filler goes, but never past the words beside it; each
23	/// edge then maps to project time through `MediaTranscript.project` (R6-10's
24	/// door) and snaps INWARD to the frame grid, as Remove Silences snaps. A
25	/// candidate that would cut into another clip's word, a nest clip or a
26	/// transition is dropped whole, never trimmed, so every kept edge is a grid
27	/// edge.
28	enum FillerDetector {
29	
30	    /// The Silero VAD's chunk in source ticks (512 samples at 16 kHz), from
31	    /// absolute source time 0 — the speech cache's own index.
32	    static var grid: Ticks { MediaSpeech.chunkTicks }
33	
34	    /// Which clips were read: the ones named or selected, or every clip.
35	    enum Scope: String { case selected, all }
36	
37	    /// One clip's job and the transcript file of its media.
38	    struct ClipWords {
39	        let job: Transcriber.Job
40	        let file: MediaTranscript.File
41	    }
42	
43	    /// Everything a detection reads, taken off the document once.
44	    struct Input {
45	        let fps: Fps
46	        let scope: Scope
47	        /// The scope's clips whose media has a transcript that asked for fillers.
48	        let clips: [ClipWords]
49	        /// Media ids in scope with no such transcript, sorted and distinct.
50	        let needsTranscript: [UInt32]
51	        /// The named clips `Transcriber.jobs` refused, each with its reason.
52	        let skipped: [CaptionLayout.Problem]
53	        /// In-scope clip ids on locked tracks, sorted: the ripple neither cuts
54	        /// nor moves a locked track, so their fillers are not read.
55	        let locked: [UInt32]
56	        /// Every top-level clip on an unlocked track whose media's transcript
57	        /// serves `.captions`, in scope or not: the ripple cuts every
58	        /// unlocked track, so their words protect a span.
59	        let neighbours: [ClipWords]
60	        let nests: [SilenceDetector.NestExtent]
61	        let walls: [SilenceDetector.Span]
62	    }
63	
64	    /// One run of consecutive fillers in a clip's word order, in source ticks.
65	    struct Run: Equatable {
66	        let words: [String]
67	        let source: SilenceDetector.Span
68	        /// The latest end of a non-filler word before the run, or the clip's `in`.
69	        let previousEnd: Ticks
70	        /// The earliest start of a non-filler word after it, or the window's end.
71	        let nextStart: Ticks
72	    }
73	
74	    /// A run that became a cut: its source span on the grid and its project span.
75	    struct Candidate: Equatable {
76	        let clip: UInt32
77	        let words: [String]
78	        let source: SilenceDetector.Span
79	        let span: SilenceDetector.Span
80	    }
81	
82	    enum DropReason: Equatable {
83	        case tooShort
84	        case overlapsWord(clip: UInt32, text: String)
85	        case nest(clip: UInt32)
86	        case transition
87	    }
88	
89	    struct Dropped: Equatable {
90	        let clip: UInt32
91	        let words: [String]
92	        let reason: DropReason
93	    }
94	
95	    struct Outcome {
96	        /// The kept candidates merged where they overlap or touch.
97	        let spans: [SilenceDetector.Span]
98	        let candidates: [Candidate]
99	        let dropped: [Dropped]
100	        let scope: Scope
101	        /// The clips whose words were read, sorted.
102	        let clips: [UInt32]
103	        let needsTranscript: [UInt32]
104	        let skipped: [CaptionLayout.Problem]
105	        let locked: [UInt32]
106	
107	        var removed: Ticks { spans.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.length } }
108	    }
109	
110	    // MARK: - The read
111	
112	    /// The document's snapshot, scope and transcript cache, read once.
113	    ///
114	    /// Named clips are the scope (`.selected`); with none named, the
115	    /// selection when `Transcriber.jobs` accepts any of it, else every clip.
116	    /// The EDITED project, as `SilenceDetector.read` takes it: with a nest
117	    /// open the ranges are the nest's, in the nest's own time.
118	    static func read(from document: ProjectDocument, clips named: [UInt32]?) -> Input {
119	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
120	        let urls = document.mediaURLs()
121	        let maps = document.editedProject.sourceMap
122	        let scope: Scope
123	        let chosen: [ClipSnapshot]
124	        if let named {
125	            let ids = Set(named)
126	            chosen = snapshot.clips.filter { ids.contains($0.id) }
127	            scope = .selected
128	        } else {
129	            let selected = snapshot.clips.filter { document.selection.contains($0.id) }
130	            if !Transcriber.jobs(for: selected, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: maps).jobs.isEmpty {
131	                chosen = selected
132	                scope = .selected
133	            } else {
134	                chosen = snapshot.clips
135	                scope = .all
136	            }
137	        }
138	        let (kept, locked) = onUnlockedTracks(chosen, in: snapshot)
139	        let (jobs, problems) = Transcriber.jobs(for: kept, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: maps)
140	        let cacheDirectory = document.cacheDirectory
141	
142	        var clips: [ClipWords] = []
143	        var needs: Set<UInt32> = []
144	        var scopeFiles: [UInt32: MediaTranscript.File?] = [:]
145	        for job in jobs {
146	            if scopeFiles[job.media] == nil {
147	                scopeFiles[job.media] = .some(
148	                    cacheDirectory.flatMap { cache in
149	                        snapshot.media(job.media).flatMap {
150	                            fillersFile(for: $0, url: job.source, in: cache)
151	                        }
152	                    })
153	            }
154	            if let file = scopeFiles[job.media] ?? nil {
155	                clips.append(ClipWords(job: job, file: file))
156	            } else {
157	                needs.insert(job.media)
158	            }
159	        }
160	
161	        var neighbours: [ClipWords] = []
162	        if let cacheDirectory {
163	            let unlocked = onUnlockedTracks(snapshot.clips, in: snapshot).kept
164	            var files: [UInt32: MediaTranscript.File?] = [:]
165	            let found = Transcriber.jobs(for: unlocked, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: maps)
166	            for job in found.jobs {
167	                if files[job.media] == nil {
168	                    files[job.media] = .some(
169	                        snapshot.media(job.media).flatMap {
170	                            transcriptFile(
171	                                for: $0, url: job.source, in: cacheDirectory, use: .captions)
172	                        })
173	                }
174	                if let file = files[job.media] ?? nil {
175	                    neighbours.append(ClipWords(job: job, file: file))
176	                }
177	            }
178	        }
179	        return Input(
180	            fps: snapshot.canvas.fps, scope: scope, clips: clips, needsTranscript: needs.sorted(),
181	            skipped: named == nil ? [] : problems, locked: locked, neighbours: neighbours,
182	            nests: SilenceDetector.nestExtents(in: snapshot),
183	            walls: SilenceDetector.overlapWalls(snapshot))
184	    }

186	    /// The scope's door: a media's transcript only when its marker serves
187	    /// filler removal (TR-7, TR-2).
188	    static func fillersFile(
189	        for media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, in cacheDir: URL
190	    ) -> MediaTranscript.File? {
191	        transcriptFile(for: media, url: url, in: cacheDir, use: .fillers)

194	    /// A media's cached transcript when the file as it is NOW stamps the
195	    /// marker's source, the file reads, and the marker serves `use` for the
196	    /// request the file records; else nil.
197	    static func transcriptFile(
198	        for media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, in cacheDir: URL, use: TranscriptUse
199	    ) -> MediaTranscript.File? {
200	        guard let stamp = MediaImporter.CacheStamp.stamp(for: media, url: url),
201	            let file = MediaTranscript.read(for: media.id, in: cacheDir),
202	            let marker = MediaTranscript.readStamp(for: media.id, in: cacheDir),
203	            marker.serves(TranscriptStamp(source: stamp, options: file.header.requested), for: use)
204	        else { return nil }
205	        return file
206	    }

208	    /// The clips not on a locked track, and the ids of those that are,
209	    /// sorted. A track the snapshot cannot find counts as unlocked, as the
210	    /// nest walls read it.
211	    static func onUnlockedTracks(
212	        _ clips: [ClipSnapshot], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot
213	    ) -> (kept: [ClipSnapshot], locked: [UInt32]) {
214	        var kept: [ClipSnapshot] = []
215	        var locked: [UInt32] = []
216	        for clip in clips {
217	            if snapshot.track(clip.track)?.locked == true {
218	                locked.append(clip.id)
219	            } else {
220	                kept.append(clip)
221	            }
222	        }
223	        return (kept, locked.sorted())
224	    }

226	    // MARK: - The arithmetic
227	
228	    /// One word of a clip's window, in source ticks.
229	    private struct Timed {
230	        let text: String
231	        let start: Ticks
232	        let end: Ticks
233	        let filler: Bool
234	    }
235	
236	    /// The clip's words in source ticks: those whose start is in its window
237	    /// (R6-10), sorted by start then end.
238	    private static func timed(_ file: MediaTranscript.File, in job: Transcriber.Job) -> [Timed] {
239	        let windowEnd = job.sourceIn + job.sourceLength
240	        var out: [Timed] = []
241	        for word in file.words {
242	            let start = MediaTranscript.sourceTicks(milliseconds: word.start)
243	            guard start >= job.sourceIn, start < windowEnd else { continue }
244	            out.append(
245	                Timed(
246	                    text: word.text, start: start,
247	                    end: MediaTranscript.sourceTicks(milliseconds: max(word.start, word.end)),
248	                    filler: FillerWords.isFiller(word.text)))
249	        }
250	        return out.sorted { ($0.start, $0.end) < ($1.start, $1.end) }
251	    }
252	
253	    /// Every maximal run of consecutive fillers in the clip's word order,
254	    /// with the non-filler words that bound it (TR-9).
255	    static func runs(of file: MediaTranscript.File, in job: Transcriber.Job) -> [Run] {
256	        let words = timed(file, in: job)
257	        let windowEnd = job.sourceIn + job.sourceLength
258	        // The latest non-filler end before each index, and the earliest
259	        // non-filler start after it.
260	        var before = [Ticks](repeating: job.sourceIn, count: words.count + 1)
261	        for (index, word) in words.enumerated() {
262	            before[index + 1] = word.filler ? before[index] : max(before[index], word.end)
263	        }
264	        var after = [Ticks](repeating: windowEnd, count: words.count + 1)
265	        for index in stride(from: words.count - 1, through: 0, by: -1) {
266	            let word = words[index]
267	            after[index] = word.filler ? after[index + 1] : min(after[index + 1], word.start)
268	        }
269	        var runs: [Run] = []
270	        var open: [Int] = []
271	        func close() {
272	            guard let first = open.first, let last = open.last else { return }
273	            runs.append(
274	                Run(
275	                    words: open.map { words[$0].text },
276	                    source: SilenceDetector.Span(
277	                        start: words[first].start, end: open.map { words[$0].end }.max() ?? 0),
278	                    previousEnd: before[first], nextStart: after[last + 1]))
279	            open = []
280	        }
281	        for (index, word) in words.enumerated() {
282	            guard word.filler else {
283	                close()
284	                continue
285	            }
286	            open.append(index)
287	        }
288	        close()
289	        return runs
290	    }

292	    private static func down(_ t: Ticks, _ grid: Ticks) -> Ticks {
293	        let q = t / grid
294	        return (t % grid != 0 && t < 0 ? q - 1 : q) * grid
295	    }
296	
297	    private static func up(_ t: Ticks, _ grid: Ticks) -> Ticks {
298	        let q = t / grid
299	        return (t % grid != 0 && t > 0 ? q + 1 : q) * grid
300	    }
301	
302	    /// A run's source span widened outward to the grid, bounded by its
303	    /// neighbours' grid points inward; nil when nothing is left.
304	    static func gridded(_ run: Run, grid: Ticks) -> SilenceDetector.Span? {
305	        guard grid > 0 else { return nil }
306	        let start = max(down(run.source.start, grid), up(run.previousEnd, grid))
307	        let end = min(up(run.source.end, grid), down(run.nextStart, grid))
308	        guard end > start else { return nil }
309	        return SilenceDetector.Span(start: start, end: end)
310	    }
311	
312	    /// A source span in project time, its start snapped up and its end down
313	    /// to the frame grid; nil when nothing is left.
314	    static func placed(
315	        _ source: SilenceDetector.Span, in job: Transcriber.Job, fps: Fps
316	    ) -> SilenceDetector.Span? {
317	        let span = SilenceDetector.Span(
318	            start: SilenceDetector.snapUpToFrame(
319	                MediaTranscript.project(source.start, in: job), fps: fps),
320	            end: SilenceDetector.snapDownToFrame(
321	                MediaTranscript.project(source.end, in: job), fps: fps))
322	        guard span.end > span.start else { return nil }
323	        return span
324	    }

326	    // MARK: - Detection
327	
328	    /// The candidates, what was dropped and why, and the merged ranges.
329	    static func detect(_ input: Input) -> Outcome {
330	        // Every neighbour's non-filler words in project time, read once.
331	        let guarded: [(clip: UInt32, words: [CaptionCues.Word])] = input.neighbours.map {
332	            ($0.job.clip,
333	             MediaTranscript.words(for: $0.job, in: $0.file).filter {
334	                 !FillerWords.isFiller($0.text)
335	             })
336	        }
337	        var candidates: [Candidate] = []
338	        var dropped: [Dropped] = []
339	        for clip in input.clips {
340	            let id = clip.job.clip
341	            for run in runs(of: clip.file, in: clip.job) {
342	                guard let source = gridded(run, grid: grid),
343	                    let span = placed(source, in: clip.job, fps: input.fps)
344	                else {
345	                    dropped.append(Dropped(clip: id, words: run.words, reason: .tooShort))
346	                    continue
347	                }
348	                if let reason = conflict(span, clip: id, guarded: guarded, input: input) {
349	                    dropped.append(Dropped(clip: id, words: run.words, reason: reason))
350	                    continue
351	                }
352	                candidates.append(Candidate(clip: id, words: run.words, source: source, span: span))
353	            }
354	        }
355	        return Outcome(
356	            spans: SilenceDetector.merged(candidates.map(\.span)), candidates: candidates,
357	            dropped: dropped, scope: input.scope,
358	            clips: Set(input.clips.map { $0.job.clip }).sorted(),
359	            needsTranscript: input.needsTranscript, skipped: input.skipped, locked: input.locked)
360	    }
361	
362	    /// Why a span may not be cut, in TR-9's order: another clip's word, a
363	    /// nest clip, a transition wall; nil when it may.
364	    private static func conflict(
365	        _ span: SilenceDetector.Span, clip: UInt32,
366	        guarded: [(clip: UInt32, words: [CaptionCues.Word])], input: Input
367	    ) -> DropReason? {
368	        for neighbour in guarded where neighbour.clip != clip {
369	            if let word = neighbour.words.first(where: {
370	                SilenceDetector.overlap(span, SilenceDetector.Span(start: $0.start, end: $0.end)) > 0
371	            }) {
372	                return .overlapsWord(clip: neighbour.clip, text: word.text)
373	            }
374	        }
375	        if let nest = input.nests.first(where: { SilenceDetector.overlap(span, $0.span) > 0 }) {
376	            return .nest(clip: nest.clip)
377	        }
378	        if input.walls.contains(where: { SilenceDetector.overlap(span, $0) > 0 }) {
379	            return .transition
380	        }
381	        return nil
382	    }
383	}

141	    /// One media's paid upload, on `CloudTranscriber.run`'s own queue, with
142	    /// the request `FillerTranscription` builds; the completion arrives on
143	    /// main and goes to `runEnded`.
144	    func transcribe(media: UInt32) {
145	        guard let document = document, let cache = cacheDirectory,
146	            let credential = AssemblyAIConfiguration.credential(
147	                store: store, environment: environment)
148	        else {
149	            NSSound.beep()
150	            return
151	        }
152	        let client: AssemblyAIClient
153	        do {
154	            client = AssemblyAIClient(
155	                base: try AssemblyAIConfiguration.baseURL(defaults: defaults),
156	                credential: credential)
157	        } catch {
158	            lastError = error.localizedDescription
159	            refresh()
160	            return
161	        }
162	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
163	        let jobs = FillerTranscription.jobs(
164	            for: media, in: snapshot, urls: document.mediaURLs(),
165	            maps: document.editedProject.sourceMap)
166	        guard !jobs.isEmpty else {
167	            NSSound.beep()
168	            return
169	        }
170	        var records: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot] = [:]
171	        for entry in snapshot.media { records[entry.id] = entry }
172	        let run = CloudTranscriber(client: client, cacheDirectory: cache, media: records)
173	        let cancel = Transcriber.CancelToken()
174	        cloud = run
175	        token = cancel
176	        runStarted(media: media)
177	        run.run(
178	            jobs: jobs,
179	            options: FillerTranscription.options(
180	                for: MediaTranscript.readStamp(for: media, in: cache)),
181	            refresh: FillerTranscription.refresh,
182	            frame: max(snapshot.canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1),
183	            pages: CaptionPages.Request(
184	                style: .subtitles,
185	                canvas: CGSize(width: snapshot.canvas.width, height: snapshot.canvas.height)),
186	            cancel: cancel,
187	            progress: { [weak self] fraction, detail in
188	                DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.progressed(media, fraction, detail) }
189	            },
190	            completion: { [weak self] outcome in
191	                guard let self = self, !self.tornDown else { return }
192	                if case .failure(let error) = outcome {
193	                    self.runEnded(error: error)
194	                } else {
195	                    self.runEnded(error: nil)
196	                }
197	            })
198	    }

200	    /// The running row's estimate line, while it runs.
201	    private func progressed(_ media: UInt32, _ fraction: Double, _ detail: String) {
202	        guard media == runningMedia, let row = mediaRows.first(where: { $0.media == media })
203	        else { return }
204	        let percent = "\(Int((min(max(fraction, 0), 1) * 100).rounded())) %"
205	        row.estimate.stringValue = (detail.isEmpty ? "Transcribing" : detail) + " · " + percent
206	    }
207	}

3	/// Remove Filler Words' re-transcribe (road map "cut-by-transcript" CT-3, spec
4	/// §11 TR-2, TR-7, TR-10): the request, the jobs and the estimate one press
5	/// of the sheet's Transcribe button sends for one media, shared by the sheet
6	/// (`FillerSheetController+Transcribe.swift`) and its mirror,
7	/// `transcribe_for_fillers` (`AgentServer+Fillers.swift`), so the two cannot
8	/// send different requests or quote different prices.
9	///
10	/// It holds no document. The jobs come from a snapshot and its media URLs,
11	/// and the estimate from a cache directory, all passed by value — which is
12	/// what lets the tool read them in one main-thread hop and run off main.
13	///
14	/// **TR-10's request.** The media's PREVIOUS request is kept — the marker's
15	/// language, speaker labels and vocabulary — so the filler transcript is the
16	/// same transcript as before with the fillers in it; the shipped models,
17	/// `disfluencies: true` and `refresh: true` are added. With no marker it is
18	/// detection, no speakers and no vocabulary. `refresh` is what makes a media
19	/// whose caption transcript is current upload again: `CloudEstimate.fate`
20	/// and `CloudTranscriber.transcribe` both judge currency for `.captions`,
21	/// which ignores `disfluencies` (TR-2).
22	enum FillerTranscription {
23	
24	    /// Always on: a media in the sheet's list has a transcript that serves
25	    /// captions or none, and either way it must be fetched again.
26	    static let refresh = true
27	
28	    /// The marker's request with fillers asked for, or detection with none.
29	    static func options(for marker: TranscriptStamp?) -> TranscriptOptions {
30	        TranscriptOptions(
31	            speechModels: TranscriptOptions.shippedModels,
32	            languageCode: marker?.languageCode,
33	            speakerLabels: marker?.speakerLabels ?? false,
34	            keytermsPrompt: marker?.keytermsPrompt ?? [],
35	            disfluencies: true)
36	    }
37	
38	    /// `Transcriber.jobs` over the snapshot's clips that play `media`; the
39	    /// clips it refuses (a reversed one, one whose audio is off, a missing
40	    /// file) are left out, as a caption run leaves them. `maps` are the
41	    /// source maps of the snapshot's handle, so a ramped clip's job follows
42	    /// its map (spec §11 SR-20 (d)).
43	    static func jobs(
44	        for media: UInt32, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, urls: [UInt32: URL], maps: SourceMaps
45	    ) -> [Transcriber.Job] {
46	        let clips = snapshot.clips.filter { clip in
47	            guard case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source else { return false }
48	            return id == media
49	        }
50	        return Transcriber.jobs(for: clips, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: maps).jobs
51	    }
52	
53	    /// What one press would upload and cost, by `CloudEstimate`'s own rules
54	    /// over the same request the run sends; nil when there is nothing to run.
55	    static func estimate(
56	        jobs: [Transcriber.Job], media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot], cacheDirectory: URL
57	    ) -> CloudEstimate? {
58	        guard !jobs.isEmpty else { return nil }
59	        let facts = CloudEstimate.facts(jobs: jobs, media: media, cacheDirectory: cacheDirectory)
60	        return CloudEstimate(
61	            facts: facts, options: options(for: facts.first?.marker), refresh: refresh)
62	    }
63	}

3	/// The one filler vocabulary (spec §11 TR-8) and the rule that matches a word
4	/// against it. Every caption producer's input passes through
5	/// `MediaTranscript.captionWords`, so a caption made from a transcript that
6	/// asked for fillers (TR-1) is the caption the same words make without them.
7	///
8	/// The cache keeps every served word verbatim (R6-3): this filters decoded
9	/// words only, and `wordsJSON` and `File.encoded()` never see it.
10	enum FillerWords {
11	
12	    /// TR-8's list: the tokens AssemblyAI itself names as fillers for the
13	    /// models the app requests. "uh huh" is matched by its two halves, and
14	    /// `uh-huh` as one token. Another source's fillers (TR-7) are added by
15	    /// that source's own entry.
16	    static let assemblyAI: Set<String> = [
17	        "um", "uh", "hmm", "mhm", "uh-huh", "ah", "huh", "hm", "m", "er", "erm",
18	    ]
19	
20	    /// Lowercased, then leading and trailing punctuation and whitespace
21	    /// trimmed: `"Um,"` is `"um"`, and an inner hyphen stays.
22	    static func normalized(_ text: String) -> String {
23	        text.lowercased().trimmingCharacters(in: trimmed)
24	    }
25	
26	    /// The set `normalized` trims, made once: building the union on every
27	    /// call was nine tenths of placing a 27,000-word timeline transcript
28	    /// (185 of 200 ms, measured for TX2a's T6).
29	    private static let trimmed = CharacterSet.punctuationCharacters.union(.whitespacesAndNewlines)
30	
31	    /// Whether a word is a filler: its normalised text is in the list.
32	    static func isFiller(_ text: String) -> Bool {
33	        assemblyAI.contains(normalized(text))
34	    }
35	}
36	
37	extension MediaTranscript {
38	
39	    /// `words(for:in:)` with every `FillerWords.isFiller` word removed; the
40	    /// order and every other word untouched. What a caption is made from.
41	    static func captionWords(for job: Transcriber.Job, in file: File) -> [CaptionCues.Word] {
42	        words(for: job, in: file).filter { !FillerWords.isFiller($0.text) }
43	    }
44	}

9	/// registers no undo step, as `detect_silence` does
10	/// (`AgentServer+Silence.swift`, whose posture this follows). The words are
11	/// a Swift cache (`cache/transcripts/`), so an agent that could only call
12	/// `ripple_delete_ranges` would have nothing to cut by; this answers the
13	/// ranges and `ripple_delete_ranges` makes the one undo step.
14	///
15	/// It stays on the MAIN thread, out of `AgentServer.offMainTools`, for
16	/// `detect_silence`'s reason: reading a few cached transcripts and one pass
17	/// of arithmetic waits on nothing and has no completion to deliver. It never
18	/// makes a network call: only a cached AssemblyAI transcript that asked for
19	/// filler words is read (TR-7). `transcribe_for_fillers` is the other
20	/// posture: a paid upload, off main (`AgentServer.offMainTools`), always
21	/// withheld from the assistant (AI-7 as TR-10 amends it).
22	extension AgentServer {
23	
24	    /// `detect_fillers` — the read half of Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…, and
25	    /// the agent's path. Nothing is edited: feed `ranges` to
26	    /// `ripple_delete_ranges` to make the cut.
27	    func detectFillers(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
28	        let document = try target(a)
29	        let clips = try optionalClipsArg(a, "clips", document)
30	        let input = FillerDetector.read(from: document, clips: clips)
31	        let outcome = FillerDetector.detect(input)
32	
33	        var result: [String: Any] = [
34	            "ok": true,
35	            "ranges": outcome.spans.map { [$0.start, $0.end] },
36	            "count": outcome.spans.count,
37	            "removes": outcome.removed,
38	            "scope": outcome.scope.rawValue,
39	            "clips": outcome.clips.map { Int($0) },
40	            "fillers": outcome.candidates.map { candidate -> [String: Any] in
41	                [
42	                    "clip": Int(candidate.clip), "words": candidate.words,
43	                    "range": [candidate.span.start, candidate.span.end],
44	                ]
45	            },
46	            "dropped": outcome.dropped.map { drop -> [String: Any] in
47	                ["clip": Int(drop.clip), "words": drop.words, "reason": Self.sentence(drop.reason)]
48	            },
49	            "needs_transcript": outcome.needsTranscript.map { Int($0) },
50	            "locked": outcome.locked.map { Int($0) },
51	        ]
52	        if clips != nil, !outcome.skipped.isEmpty {
53	            result["skipped"] = outcome.skipped.map { $0.description }
54	        }
55	        var notes: [String] = []
56	        if outcome.clips.isEmpty, outcome.needsTranscript.isEmpty, outcome.locked.isEmpty {
57	            notes.append("Nothing in scope plays speech from a media file, so nothing was read.")
58	        }
59	        if !outcome.needsTranscript.isEmpty {
60	            notes.append(
61	                "Media \(Self.fillerList(outcome.needsTranscript)) has no transcript made with "
62	                    + "filler words, so its fillers cannot be found: filler removal needs an "
63	                    + "AssemblyAI transcript (spec §11 TR-7). transcribe_for_fillers makes "
64	                    + "one for a media, keeping its earlier request (a paid upload).")
65	        }
66	        if !outcome.locked.isEmpty {
67	            notes.append(
68	                "Clip \(Self.fillerList(outcome.locked)) is on a locked track, which "
69	                    + "ripple_delete_ranges neither cuts nor moves, so its fillers were not read.")
70	        }
71	        if !notes.isEmpty { result["note"] = notes.joined(separator: " ") }
72	        result["project"] = summary(document)
73	        return try jsonResult(result)
74	    }

76	    /// `transcribe_for_fillers` — the Transcribe button of Clip ▸ Remove
77	    /// Filler Words…' rows (`FillerSheetController+Transcribe.swift`): one
78	    /// media re-transcribed with AssemblyAI, with its previous request plus
79	    /// filler words (`FillerTranscription`, TR-10). Only the media's
80	    /// transcript cache is written: no caption is placed, no undo step made.
81	    ///
82	    /// Refused in this order, every step above the network: the media id,
83	    /// a document with nowhere to keep the cache, a media no clip plays from
84	    /// its file, then the credential; a media that already has a filler
85	    /// transcript answers with no request, between the last two.
86	    func transcribeForFillers(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
87	        guard !Thread.isMainThread else {
88	            throw ToolError(
89	                message: "transcribe_for_fillers must run on the server thread — its name is "
90	                    + "missing from AgentServer.offMainTools.")
91	        }
92	        struct Context {
93	            let document: ProjectDocument
94	            let media: UInt32
95	            let cache: URL
96	            let jobs: [Transcriber.Job]
97	            let records: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot]
98	            let ready: Bool
99	            let frame: Ticks
100	            let canvas: CGSize
101	        }
102	        let context = try onMain { () -> Context in
103	            let document = try self.target(a)
104	            let media = try self.mediaArg(a, "media", document)
105	            guard let cache = document.cacheDirectory else {
106	                throw ToolError(
107	                    message: "This document has nowhere to keep its transcript cache, so it "
108	                        + "cannot be transcribed with AssemblyAI. Save it first.")
109	            }
110	            let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
111	            let jobs = FillerTranscription.jobs(
112	                for: media.id, in: snapshot, urls: document.mediaURLs(),
113	                maps: document.editedProject.sourceMap)
114	            guard let first = jobs.first else {
115	                throw ToolError(
116	                    message: "No clip in this timeline plays media \(media.id) from its file, so "
117	                        + "it cannot be transcribed.")
118	            }
119	            var records: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot] = [:]
120	            for entry in snapshot.media { records[entry.id] = entry }
121	            return Context(
122	                document: document, media: media.id, cache: cache, jobs: jobs, records: records,
123	                ready: Self.fillersReady(media, url: first.source, cache: cache),
124	                frame: max(snapshot.canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1),
125	                canvas: CGSize(width: snapshot.canvas.width, height: snapshot.canvas.height))
126	        }
127	        let options = FillerTranscription.options(
128	            for: MediaTranscript.readStamp(for: context.media, in: context.cache))
129	
130	        var result: [String: Any]
131	        if context.ready {
132	            var report = CloudTranscriber.Report()
133	            report.cached = [context.media]
134	            result = Self.cloudFields(
135	                report, code: options.languageCode, endpoint: nil,
136	                notes: [
137	                    "Media \(context.media) already has a transcript made with filler words, so "
138	                        + "nothing was uploaded."
139	                ])
140	            result["ready"] = true
141	        } else {
142	            guard
143	                let credential = AssemblyAIConfiguration.credential(
144	                    store: AssemblyAIConfiguration.store())
145	            else {
146	                throw ModelKeys.refusal(.assemblyAI)
147	            }
148	            let client: AssemblyAIClient
149	            do {
150	                client = AssemblyAIClient(
151	                    base: try AssemblyAIConfiguration.baseURL(), credential: credential)
152	            } catch {
153	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
154	            }
155	            let transcriber = CloudTranscriber(
156	                client: client, cacheDirectory: context.cache, media: context.records)
157	            do {
158	                _ = try transcriber.transcribe(
159	                    context.jobs, options: options, refresh: FillerTranscription.refresh,
160	                    frame: context.frame,
161	                    pages: CaptionPages.Request(style: .subtitles, canvas: context.canvas),
162	                    cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken())
163	            } catch {
164	                throw ToolError(message: Self.cloudFailure(error, report: transcriber.report))
165	            }
166	            result = Self.cloudFields(
167	                transcriber.report, code: options.languageCode, endpoint: client.base.host,
168	                notes: [])
169	        }
170	        return try onMain {
171	            if !context.ready {
172	                // Asked again: the run's answer is what the cache holds now.
173	                let media = context.document.editedProject.snapshot.media(context.media)
174	                result["ready"] = media.map {
175	                    Self.fillersReady($0, url: context.jobs[0].source, cache: context.cache)
176	                } ?? false
177	            }
178	            result["ok"] = true
179	            result["media"] = Int(context.media)
180	            result["project"] = self.summary(context.document)
181	            return try self.jsonResult(result)
182	        }
183	    }
184	
185	    /// Whether the media now has a transcript `FillerDetector` reads.
186	    private static func fillersReady(_ media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, cache: URL) -> Bool {
187	        FillerDetector.fillersFile(for: media, url: url, in: cache) != nil
188	    }
189	
190	    /// A drop reason as the answer's sentence.
191	    private static func sentence(_ reason: FillerDetector.DropReason) -> String {
192	        switch reason {
193	        case .tooShort:
194	            return "too short to cut once its edges are on the 32 ms grid and the frame grid"
195	        case .overlapsWord(let clip, let text):
196	            return "it overlaps \"\(text)\" in clip \(clip)"
197	        case .nest(let clip):
198	            return "it crosses nest clip \(clip), which a cut must not split"
199	        case .transition:
200	            return "it crosses a transition"
201	        }
202	    }
203	
204	    /// "3, 7, 9".
205	    private static func fillerList(_ ids: [UInt32]) -> String {
206	        ids.map { String($0) }.joined(separator: ", ")
207	    }
208	}

1	import CoreML
2	import Foundation
3	
4	/// Silero VAD v6.2.1 through Core ML: the streaming 32 ms wrapper road map
5	/// 4's S0 spike proved and S1 ships. No AppKit, no `async` — the model
6	/// predicts synchronously, which is what lets `SilenceDetector.detect`
7	/// (never off main) and `MediaImporter+Speech.writeSpeech` (which never
8	/// `await`s) share one class.
9	///
10	/// `tools/proof/silence_spike/silero_coreml.swift`'s `Silero` made streaming:
11	/// the spike's `run` fed a whole signal and returned; `feed` holds the
12	/// remainder across calls, so a reader handing it one `CMSampleBuffer` at a
13	/// time never loses the tail of a chunk that straddled two buffers.
14	///
15	/// One instance holds one utterance's state — `h`, `c`, the 64-sample
16	/// context and the held remainder — so two media analysed concurrently
17	/// (`generateCaches`'s per-media passes run in call order, but two DIFFERENT
18	/// media can overlap) each need their own `bundled()`.
19	final class SileroVAD {
20	    static let modelName = "silero-vad-6.2.1-coreml-fp16-32ms"
21	
22	    static let sampleRate = 16_000
23	    static let chunkSamples = 512
24	    static let contextSamples = 64
25	    static let stateSize = 128
26	
27	    static let audioInput = "audio"
28	    static let stateH = "h"
29	    static let stateC = "c"
30	    static let probabilityOutput = "probability"
31	    static let stateHOut = "h_out"
32	    static let stateCOut = "c_out"
33	
34	    // MARK: - Availability
35	
36	    /// The bundled model's compiled location, or nil when this build carries
37	    /// none: `Bundle.main`'s own `Models` subdirectory first (the shipped
38	    /// app), then `bundleURL/Models/silero_vad.mlmodelc` for a binary that is
39	    /// not a proper bundle (the offscreen harness, which copies `Models`
40	    /// beside itself rather than building a bundle).
41	    static var bundledURL: URL? {
42	        if let url = Bundle.main.url(
43	            forResource: "silero_vad", withExtension: "mlmodelc", subdirectory: "Models") {
44	            return url
45	        }
46	        let sibling = Bundle.main.bundleURL
47	            .appendingPathComponent("Models", isDirectory: true)
48	            .appendingPathComponent("silero_vad.mlmodelc", isDirectory: true)
49	        return FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: sibling.path) ? sibling : nil
50	    }
51	
52	    private static let availabilityLock = NSLock()
53	    private static var unavailableReason: String?
54	
55	    /// Whether the voice model can be asked for this process. `NSLock`-guarded
56	    /// because it is written from a cache pass off main (`writeSpeech`) and
57	    /// read on main (`Input.read`) — the same shape road map 3's recorder
58	    /// gives its availability flag, and `app/CLAUDE.md`'s one sanctioned
59	    /// cross-thread lock.
60	    static var isAvailable: Bool {
61	        availabilityLock.lock()
62	        defer { availabilityLock.unlock() }
63	        return bundledURL != nil && unavailableReason == nil
64	    }
65	
66	    /// Marks the model unavailable for the rest of the process. Idempotent —
67	    /// only the FIRST reason is kept and logged, because a second failure
68	    /// after the first has nothing new to say and a log line per media would
69	    /// drown the one that mattered.
70	    static func markUnavailable(_ reason: String) {
71	        availabilityLock.lock()
72	        let first = unavailableReason == nil
73	        if first { unavailableReason = reason }
74	        availabilityLock.unlock()
75	        if first { print("Frame Job: voice model unavailable — \(reason)") }
76	    }
77	
78	    /// A fresh instance, or nil (and `markUnavailable`d) for a nil URL or a
79	    /// throwing init. FRESH per call, never shared: state is per instance,
80	    /// and passes for different media run concurrently.
81	    static func bundled() -> SileroVAD? {
82	        guard let url = bundledURL else {
83	            markUnavailable("no model in the bundle")
84	            return nil
85	        }
86	        do {
87	            return try SileroVAD(modelURL: url)
88	        } catch {
89	            markUnavailable("\(error)")
90	            return nil
91	        }
92	    }
93	
94	    // MARK: - Instance
95	
96	    private let model: MLModel
97	    private var h: MLMultiArray
98	    private var c: MLMultiArray
99	    private var context: [Float]
100	    private var remainder: [Float] = []
101	
102	    init(modelURL: URL) throws {
103	        let configuration = MLModelConfiguration()
104	        configuration.computeUnits = .cpuAndNeuralEngine
105	        model = try MLModel(contentsOf: modelURL, configuration: configuration)
106	        h = try MLMultiArray(shape: [1, 1, NSNumber(value: Self.stateSize)], dataType: .float16)
107	        c = try MLMultiArray(shape: [1, 1, NSNumber(value: Self.stateSize)], dataType: .float16)
108	        for i in 0..<Self.stateSize {
109	            h[i] = 0
110	            c[i] = 0
111	        }
112	        context = [Float](repeating: 0, count: Self.contextSamples)
113	    }
114	
115	    /// Zeroes the state and drops the held context and remainder — the start
116	    /// of a fresh utterance.
117	    func reset() {
118	        for i in 0..<Self.stateSize {
119	            h[i] = 0
120	            c[i] = 0
121	        }
122	        context = [Float](repeating: 0, count: Self.contextSamples)
123	        remainder = []
124	    }
125	
126	    /// One probability per COMPLETE 512-sample chunk `samples` completes,
127	    /// counting whatever `feed` and `flush` held from earlier calls. Any
128	    /// samples left over after the last full chunk are held for next time
129	    /// (or for `flush`).
130	    func feed(_ samples: [Float]) throws -> [Float] {
131	        var pending = remainder + samples
132	        remainder = []
133	        var probabilities: [Float] = []
134	        var offset = 0
135	        while offset + Self.chunkSamples <= pending.count {
136	            let chunk = Array(pending[offset..<(offset + Self.chunkSamples)])
137	            probabilities.append(try step(chunk))
138	            offset += Self.chunkSamples
139	        }
140	        remainder = Array(pending[offset...])
141	        pending = []
142	        return probabilities
143	    }
144	
145	    /// The held remainder, zero-padded to a full chunk and run once — or nil
146	    /// when nothing was held.
147	    func flush() throws -> Float? {
148	        guard !remainder.isEmpty else { return nil }
149	        var chunk = remainder
150	        chunk.append(contentsOf: [Float](repeating: 0, count: Self.chunkSamples - chunk.count))
151	        remainder = []
152	        return try step(chunk)
153	    }
154	
155	    /// `reset` + `feed` + `flush`: the whole signal, one call, the spike's
156	    /// `run` with the tail folded in.
157	    func probabilities(of samples: [Float]) throws -> [Float] {
158	        reset()
159	        var result = try feed(samples)
160	        if let tail = try flush() { result.append(tail) }
161	        return result
162	    }
163	
164	    /// One 512-sample chunk through the model: 64 samples of context + the
165	    /// new 512 as `[1,1,576]`, `h`/`c` fed back, the context updated to the
166	    /// chunk's last 64 samples.
167	    private func step(_ chunk: [Float]) throws -> Float {
168	        let width = Self.contextSamples + Self.chunkSamples
169	        let audio = try MLMultiArray(shape: [1, 1, NSNumber(value: width)], dataType: .float16)
170	        audio.withUnsafeMutableBytes { raw, _ in
171	            let pointer = raw.bindMemory(to: Float16.self)
172	            for i in 0..<Self.contextSamples { pointer[i] = Float16(context[i]) }
173	            for i in 0..<Self.chunkSamples { pointer[Self.contextSamples + i] = Float16(chunk[i]) }
174	        }
175	        let input = try MLDictionaryFeatureProvider(dictionary: [
176	            Self.audioInput: audio, Self.stateH: h, Self.stateC: c,
177	        ])
178	        let output = try model.prediction(from: input)
179	        guard
180	            let probabilityValue = output.featureValue(for: Self.probabilityOutput)?
181	                .multiArrayValue,
182	            let hOut = output.featureValue(for: Self.stateHOut)?.multiArrayValue,
183	            let cOut = output.featureValue(for: Self.stateCOut)?.multiArrayValue
184	        else {
185	            throw SileroError.badOutput
186	        }
187	        h = hOut
188	        c = cOut
189	        context = Array(chunk[(Self.chunkSamples - Self.contextSamples)...])
190	        return Float(truncating: probabilityValue[0])
191	    }
192	
193	    private enum SileroError: Error, CustomStringConvertible {
194	        case badOutput
195	        var description: String { "the model's output did not carry the expected features" }
196	    }
197	}

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// The cached Silero VAD probabilities — `cache/speech/<id>.bin` — and how to
4	/// ask them about a window, `MediaPeaks`' shape for the voice cache.
5	///
6	/// One 32-bit float per 512-sample chunk at 16 kHz (`SileroVAD.chunkSamples`
7	/// / `SileroVAD.sampleRate`), which is `chunkTicks` ticks of SOURCE time —
8	/// exactly 19,200, and written as the division rather than as the number for
9	/// the same reason `MediaPeaks.bucketTicks` is. `MediaPeaks.window` already
10	/// generalises the project-time → bucket-index arithmetic over the bucket
11	/// size, and `MediaPeaks.peak` takes the max over it on any grid, so this
12	/// file adds only the chunk grid, its loader and the question
13	/// `SilenceDetector`'s voice test asks.
14	enum MediaSpeech {
15	
16	    /// One probability's worth of source time, in ticks. Written as the
17	    /// division: `SileroVAD.sampleRate` and `SileroVAD.chunkSamples` each
18	    /// have exactly one home.
19	    static var chunkTicks: Ticks {
20	        ReelTime.perSecond * Ticks(SileroVAD.chunkSamples) / Ticks(SileroVAD.sampleRate)
21	    }
22	
23	    /// How many probabilities a file of `duration` produces — `writeSpeech`'s
24	    /// output length, so a caller can size the zero-filled buffer before any
25	    /// chunk lands.
26	    static func chunkCount(duration: Ticks) -> Int {
27	        max(1, Int((Double(duration) / Double(chunkTicks)).rounded(.up)))
28	    }
29	
30	    /// One media's cached probabilities read at most once, however many
31	    /// segments cite it — a `MediaCacheLoader` over `loadSpeech` instead of
32	    /// `loadPeaks`.
33	    static func loader(cacheDirectory: URL?) -> MediaCacheLoader<[Float]> {
34	        MediaCacheLoader(cacheDirectory: cacheDirectory) {
35	            MediaImporter.loadSpeech(for: $0, in: $1)
36	        }
37	    }
38	
39	    /// The loudest — here, most confident — probability the project span
40	    /// `[from, to)` of `segment` covers, or 0 when it falls outside the
41	    /// window the cache was built from: `MediaPeaks.peak` asked on the chunk
42	    /// grid.
43	    static func speechMax(
44	        _ p: [Float], over segment: PlanSegment, from: Ticks, to: Ticks, reversedPivot: Ticks?
45	    ) -> Float {
46	        MediaPeaks.peak(
47	            p, over: segment, from: from, to: to, reversedPivot: reversedPivot,
48	            bucketTicks: chunkTicks)
49	    }
50	}

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Remove Filler Words' detector (road map "cut-by-transcript" CT-2, spec §11
4	/// TR-4, TR-7, TR-9): a clip's cached cloud filler words as project ranges
5	/// `ripple_delete_ranges` cuts, every edge on the Silero 32 ms grid and then
6	/// on the frame grid.
7	///
8	/// `SilenceDetector`'s shape: `read(from:clips:)` is the one seam that touches
9	/// a document — its snapshot, its selection, its media URLs and the transcript
10	/// cache, read ONCE — and everything after it (`runs`, `gridded`, `placed`,
11	/// `detect`) is arithmetic over values. The words are a Swift cache like the
12	/// peaks (spec §7), so nothing here crosses the FFI.
13	///
14	/// **Only a transcript that asked for fillers is read** (TR-7): the scope's
15	/// files come through `fillersFile`, whose marker must serve `.fillers`
16	/// (TR-2's one rule, `TranscriptStamp.serves`). A media without one is named
17	/// in `needsTranscript` and gives no candidate. The NEIGHBOURS' words — which
18	/// protect a span from a cut — are taken from any transcript that serves
19	/// `.captions`, because a word is a word whichever request heard it.
20	///
21	/// **TR-9, the edges.** A run of consecutive fillers is widened OUTWARD to the
22	/// grid so the whole filler goes, but never past the words beside it; each
23	/// edge then maps to project time through `MediaTranscript.project` (R6-10's
24	/// door) and snaps INWARD to the frame grid, as Remove Silences snaps. A
25	/// candidate that would cut into another clip's word, a nest clip or a
26	/// transition is dropped whole, never trimmed, so every kept edge is a grid
27	/// edge.
28	enum FillerDetector {
29	
30	    /// The Silero VAD's chunk in source ticks (512 samples at 16 kHz), from
31	    /// absolute source time 0 — the speech cache's own index.
32	    static var grid: Ticks { MediaSpeech.chunkTicks }
33	
34	    /// Which clips were read: the ones named or selected, or every clip.
35	    enum Scope: String { case selected, all }
36	
37	    /// One clip's job and the transcript file of its media.
38	    struct ClipWords {
39	        let job: Transcriber.Job
40	        let file: MediaTranscript.File
41	    }
42	
43	    /// Everything a detection reads, taken off the document once.
44	    struct Input {
45	        let fps: Fps
46	        let scope: Scope
47	        /// The scope's clips whose media has a transcript that asked for fillers.
48	        let clips: [ClipWords]
49	        /// Media ids in scope with no such transcript, sorted and distinct.
50	        let needsTranscript: [UInt32]
51	        /// The named clips `Transcriber.jobs` refused, each with its reason.
52	        let skipped: [CaptionLayout.Problem]
53	        /// In-scope clip ids on locked tracks, sorted: the ripple neither cuts
54	        /// nor moves a locked track, so their fillers are not read.
55	        let locked: [UInt32]
56	        /// Every top-level clip on an unlocked track whose media's transcript
57	        /// serves `.captions`, in scope or not: the ripple cuts every
58	        /// unlocked track, so their words protect a span.
59	        let neighbours: [ClipWords]
60	        let nests: [SilenceDetector.NestExtent]
61	        let walls: [SilenceDetector.Span]
62	    }
63	
64	    /// One run of consecutive fillers in a clip's word order, in source ticks.
65	    struct Run: Equatable {
66	        let words: [String]
67	        let source: SilenceDetector.Span
68	        /// The latest end of a non-filler word before the run, or the clip's `in`.
69	        let previousEnd: Ticks
70	        /// The earliest start of a non-filler word after it, or the window's end.
71	        let nextStart: Ticks
72	    }
73	
74	    /// A run that became a cut: its source span on the grid and its project span.
75	    struct Candidate: Equatable {
76	        let clip: UInt32
77	        let words: [String]
78	        let source: SilenceDetector.Span
79	        let span: SilenceDetector.Span
80	    }
81	
82	    enum DropReason: Equatable {
83	        case tooShort
84	        case overlapsWord(clip: UInt32, text: String)
85	        case nest(clip: UInt32)
86	        case transition
87	    }
88	
89	    struct Dropped: Equatable {
90	        let clip: UInt32
91	        let words: [String]
92	        let reason: DropReason
93	    }
94	
95	    struct Outcome {
96	        /// The kept candidates merged where they overlap or touch.
97	        let spans: [SilenceDetector.Span]
98	        let candidates: [Candidate]
99	        let dropped: [Dropped]
100	        let scope: Scope
101	        /// The clips whose words were read, sorted.
102	        let clips: [UInt32]
103	        let needsTranscript: [UInt32]
104	        let skipped: [CaptionLayout.Problem]
105	        let locked: [UInt32]
106	
107	        var removed: Ticks { spans.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.length } }
